verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve a regulated entity taking a compliance step connected to digital/ICT regulatory oversight, but that is only a broad triggering context, not the same operational duty.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires carrying out an ICT testing programme involving specified technical and security tests, whereas Norm B requires a conformity-assessment body to submit an application for notification to the competent notifying authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions are substantively different: performance of technical ICT resilience testing versus submission of a notification application.
verdict.evidence_span_a: voorziet, overeenkomstig de criteria in artikel 4, lid 2, in de uitvoering van passende tests, zoals kwetsbaarheidsbeoordelingen en -scans, opensourceanalyses, netwerkbeveiligingsbeoordelingen, kloofanalyses, beoordelingen van fysieke beveiliging, vragenlijsten en scanningsoftwareoplossingen, beoordelingen van broncodes indien mogelijk, scenariogebaseerde tests, compatibiliteitstests, prestatietests, eind-tot-eindtests en penetratietests
verdict.evidence_span_b: dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require regulated entities to take proactive measures addressing digital/ICT security or resilience risks.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires implementing technical, operational, and organisational security-risk controls to limit the consequences of security incidents. Norm B requires non-micro financial entities to establish, maintain, and evaluate a comprehensive, risk-based programme for testing digital operational resilience, including assessments and other testing activities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The obligations differ in their operative compliance action: security-risk mitigation controls versus creation and operation of a resilience-testing programme.
verdict.evidence_span_a: nemen bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur vastgestelde technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van hun netwerken of diensten te beheersen
verdict.evidence_span_b: voor het vaststellen, handhaven en evalueren van een degelijk en alomvattend programma voor het testen van de digitale operationele weerbaarheid

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve reporting incidents, but they do not require the same practical compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires financial entities to establish and implement an ongoing ICT-incident management process, including detection, classification, response, escalation, communication, and reporting. Norm B requires the provider or deployer of a high-risk AI system to make a specific report of a serious incident, subject to an immediate/ten-day deadline in the case of death.
verdict.criterion_fired: The obligations differ in substance: a standing incident-management system versus an individual serious-incident notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer
verdict.evidence_span_b: de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational communication in response to a security or ICT incident, but they require different communications and different recipients.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the electronic communications service provider to notify the Dutch data-protection authority promptly about a qualifying personal-data security breach. Norm B requires the financial entity to designate a person to implement its ICT-incident communications strategy and act as spokesperson to the public and media.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action, recipient, and function differ materially: regulatory breach notification to a supervisory authority versus appointing and assigning a public/media spokesperson.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ten minste één persoon in de financiële entiteit wordt belast met de uitvoering van de communicatiestrategie voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en vervult daartoe de rol van woordvoerder bij het publiek en de media.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms regulate conduct following a risk-related triggering event, but they require different operational actions: Norm A requires the designated entity to use only products or services from permitted suppliers, excluding a minister-designated risky party; Norm B requires reporting a serious incident to the designated national competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a supplier/product-use restriction or replacement obligation, whereas Norm B imposes an incident-notification obligation to a public authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions are substantively different in practice: procurement/use restriction versus regulatory incident reporting.
verdict.evidence_span_a: uitsluitend gebruik te maken van producten of diensten van anderen dan de daarbij door Onze Minister die het aangaat genoemde partij
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to communicate specified information to a public oversight body in connection with a triggering event or completed assessment.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to send an early warning about a significant incident to both its CSIRT and competent authority, urgently and normally within 24 hours, with specified incident-related details. Norm B requires an AI deployer to notify the market surveillance authority of the results of a completed fundamental-rights impact assessment and submit a completed template; it has no stated short deadline and may be subject to an exemption.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required communications differ in substantive purpose, content, recipients, and timing: incident early-warning versus post-assessment results notification with a template.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zodra de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde beoordeling is uitgevoerd, stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to take a compliance action following an ICT/security incident: Norm A requires submitting a prescribed final (or, where the incident continues, interim) report; Norm B requires performing controls and reconciliations during incident recovery to preserve data integrity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The substantive actions differ: Norm A is an external reporting and information-submission duty to the CSIRT and competent authority, with specified content and timing. Norm B is an internal operational control duty during recovery or data reconstruction, aimed at maintaining consistency and the highest level of data integrity.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions have different objects, recipients, and practical purposes: reporting an incident and its mitigation to authorities versus conducting recovery-stage data-integrity checks.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen
verdict.evidence_span_b: verrichten financiële entiteiten de benodigde controles, ook meerdere controles, waaronder afstemmingen, om ervoor te zorgen dat het hoogste niveau van gegevensintegriteit wordt gehandhaafd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to maintain an ongoing compliance-related record or program concerning digital/ICT risks: Norm A requires maintaining an overview of personal-data breaches, while Norm B requires establishing, maintaining, and evaluating a comprehensive digital-operational-resilience testing program.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a record-keeping duty covering all personal-data breaches and specified facts/data. Norm B is a substantive governance and testing-program duty, including establishment, maintenance, evaluation, and risk-based execution of resilience tests; it is not merely an incident register.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: maintaining an incident overview versus operating and governing a comprehensive digital-resilience testing program.
verdict.evidence_span_a: houdt een overzicht bij van alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: voor het vaststellen, handhaven en evalueren van een degelijk en alomvattend programma voor het testen van de digitale operationele weerbaarheid

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met gegevensverwerking en gegevensbescherming, maar leggen niet dezelfde concrete compliance-actie op.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A legt een aansprakelijkheids- en schadevergoedingsgevolg op aan verwerkingsverantwoordelijken en onder omstandigheden verwerkers wanneer verwerking in strijd met de AVG schade veroorzaakt. Norm B verplicht financiële entiteiten vooraf passende ICT-technologieën en -processen te gebruiken om beschikbaarheids-, authenticiteits-, integriteits-, vertrouwelijkheids- en gegevensverliesrisico’s te voorkomen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen verschillen wezenlijk in aard en timing van de verplichting: A is een ex post aansprakelijkheidsregel die schadevergoeding verschuldigd maakt, terwijl B een ex ante preventieve beveiligingsverplichting voorschrijft.
verdict.evidence_span_a: is aansprakelijk voor de schade die wordt veroorzaakt door verwerking die inbreuk maakt op deze verordening
verdict.evidence_span_b: voorkomen een gebrek aan beschikbaarheid, de aantasting van de authenticiteit en integriteit, de inbreuken op de vertrouwelijkheid en het verlies van gegevens

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to an incident by creating or submitting incident-related information to an authority or designated body.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the controller to document every personal-data breach, including facts, consequences, and corrective measures, so the supervisory authority can verify compliance. Norm B requires specified financial-sector entities to make a regulatory or voluntary ICT-incident notification additionally to the designated sectoral CSIRT. Documentation for supervisory inspection and an additional incident report to a CSIRT are distinct obligations.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action and recipient differ in substance: internal/compliance documentation of personal-data breaches for supervisory verification versus transmission of an ICT-incident notification to a designated CSIRT.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms are triggered in the context of a personal-data breach or unlawful processing and concern entities involved in handling personal data.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires notifying the supervisory authority and affected individual(s), with specified information about the breach and mitigation measures. Norm B imposes substantive civil liability to compensate damage caused by processing that infringes the GDPR, subject to the stated controller/processor conditions.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required real-world compliance actions are substantively different: breach notification and content disclosure versus liability for, and potential compensation of, damage caused by unlawful processing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving aan de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens en de persoon wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft, omvat in ieder geval de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de instanties waar meer informatie over de inbreuk kan worden verkregen en de aanbevolen maatregelen om de negatieve gevolgen van de inbreuk te beperken.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elke verwerkingsverantwoordelijke die bij verwerking is betrokken, is aansprakelijk voor de schade die wordt veroorzaakt door verwerking die inbreuk maakt op deze verordening.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to take a legally mandated compliance step, but the steps are materially different: Norm A requires implementing a comprehensive, risk-based cybersecurity protection framework with specified minimum measures, whereas Norm B requires submitting an application for designation to a competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing substantive cybersecurity-management and protection obligation; Norm B is a procedural filing obligation to seek designation as a conformity-assessment body.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required real-world compliance actions are not substantially the same: implementing cybersecurity controls and policies versus filing a designation request.
verdict.evidence_span_a: zijn gebaseerd op een benadering die alle gevaren omvat en tot doel heeft netwerk- en informatiesystemen en de fysieke omgeving van die systemen tegen incidenten te beschermen, en omvatten ten minste het volgende
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern obligations triggered by an ICT incident or abnormal activity and addressed to regulated entities, but their required compliance actions are materially different.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires submission of a substantive incident progress report instead of a final report when the incident is ongoing, followed by a final report within one month after resolution. Norm B requires financial entities to maintain and regularly test mechanisms for detecting abnormal activities, ICT-network performance issues, ICT-related incidents, and physical single points of failure; it is a standing detection-capability obligation, not a reporting obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative compliance actions differ in substance: incident reporting with specified content and deadlines versus establishing and testing detection mechanisms.
verdict.evidence_span_a: dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken over mechanismen om overeenkomstig artikel 17 afwijkende activiteiten zo spoedig mogelijk te detecteren

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met een gebeurtenis die tot gevolgen voor betrokken personen of partijen kan leiden, maar zij vereisen niet dezelfde compliance-actie.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A verleent een benadeelde persoon een recht om schadevergoeding te ontvangen van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of verwerker. Norm B verplicht financiële entiteiten vooraf crisiscommunicatieplannen te hebben waarmee zij ernstige ICT-incidenten of kwetsbaarheden verantwoord bekendmaken aan cliënten, tegenpartijen en eventueel het publiek. Het gaat dus om compensatie na schade versus organisatorische voorbereiding en communicatie.
verdict.criterion_fired: De vereiste handeling, het doel en de geadresseerde van de verplichting verschillen wezenlijk: schadevergoeding ontvangen tegenover crisiscommunicatie plannen en uitvoeren.
verdict.evidence_span_a: heeft het recht om van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker schadevergoeding te ontvangen voor de geleden schade
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken financiële entiteiten over crisiscommunicatieplannen die het mogelijk maken ten minste ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten of kwetsbaarheden op verantwoordelijke wijze bekend te maken

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to report information about serious incidents to designated public authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires financial entities to submit formal initial, interim, and final reports on serious ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority under a prescribed reporting framework and timelines. Norm B requires providers of systemically risky general-purpose AI models to keep and document information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures and report it without delay to the AI Office and, where appropriate, national competent authorities. The duties differ in the regulated subject matter, reporting recipients, and—most importantly—Norm B expressly combines recordkeeping/documentation with urgent reporting of corrective-measure information, whereas Norm A is a structured incident-notification and reporting regime.
verdict.criterion_fired: The shared incident-reporting element is not the same compliance action in substance because the reporting regimes have materially different content and procedural scope.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide bepalingen houden verband met gevolgen van een normschending of incident, maar zij leggen niet dezelfde praktische compliancehandeling op.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A verleent de benadeelde persoon een civielrechtelijk recht om schadevergoeding te ontvangen van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of verwerker. Norm B bepaalt dat financiële entiteiten verantwoordelijk blijven voor de behandeling en gevolgen van gemelde ICT-incidenten, ondanks eventuele feedback van toezichthouders; het schept geen recht op schadevergoeding.
verdict.criterion_fired: De vereiste actie en juridische functie verschillen wezenlijk: compensatie aan een benadeelde versus voortdurende operationele verantwoordelijkheid voor incidentafhandeling en gevolgen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: heeft het recht om van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker schadevergoeding te ontvangen voor de geleden schade
verdict.evidence_span_b: blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating about ICT/cyber incidents or threats to an external audience.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the entity to promptly inform potentially affected service recipients about measures they can take in response to a significant cyber threat, and where necessary about the threat itself. Norm B requires appointing at least one person within the financial entity to implement the ICT-incident communication strategy and act as spokesperson to the public and media. The former is an urgent, actionable warning to potentially affected recipients; the latter is an internal role-assignment and spokesperson-governance obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action differs in substance: recipient-directed threat/mitigation information versus designation of a communications officer and spokesperson role.
verdict.evidence_span_a: deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ten minste één persoon in de financiële entiteit wordt belast met de uitvoering van de communicatiestrategie voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en vervult daartoe de rol van woordvoerder bij het publiek en de media.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating incident-related information to external public authorities. However, Norm A requires a formal incident progress report or final report containing specified incident details and mitigation information, while Norm B requires maintaining and documenting information about serious incidents and corrective measures and reporting it without delay.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a structured, deadline-based reporting duty tied to the incident’s status: a progress report replaces the final report if the incident continues, followed by a final report within one month after resolution. Norm B is an ongoing record-keeping and urgent-reporting obligation concerning serious incidents and possible corrective measures, addressed to the AI Office and, where applicable, national authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ substantively: Norm A requires submission of a prescribed progress/final incident report on a defined timetable, whereas Norm B requires maintaining and documenting information and reporting it without delay.
verdict.evidence_span_a: dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require regulated entities to implement and maintain technical/organizational capabilities addressing ICT or network security risks and incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires broad, risk-proportionate preventive security measures to manage service-security risks and minimize incident consequences, potentially including encryption. Norm B specifically requires financial entities to have mechanisms for rapid detection of anomalous activity, ICT performance issues, ICT incidents, and physical single points of failure, with regular testing.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action differs in substance: broad preventive risk-management and impact-mitigation measures versus specific rapid-detection mechanisms and their testing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: nemen passende en evenredige technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van hun diensten te beheersen, waaronder in voorkomend geval versleuteling, teneinde de gevolgen van beveiligingsincidenten op gebruikers en op andere netwerken en diensten zo laag mogelijk te houden
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken over mechanismen om overeenkomstig artikel 17 afwijkende activiteiten zo spoedig mogelijk te detecteren, met inbegrip van kwesties op het gebied van ICT-netwerkprestaties en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, en om potentiële zwakke fysieke punten (“single points of failure”) te identificeren

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require regulated providers to take measures addressing risks associated with serious security or cyber incidents affecting their systems or services.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a broad, ongoing risk-management duty to implement proportionate technical, operational, and organisational security measures, potentially including encryption, to reduce incident impacts. Norm B imposes a specific AI-model duty to maintain, document, and promptly report information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures to designated authorities; its separate cybersecurity requirement concerns the AI model and physical infrastructure.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative compliance actions are materially different: preventive security-risk controls under A versus incident-information recordkeeping, documentation, and urgent regulatory reporting under B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: nemen passende en evenredige technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van hun diensten te beheersen, waaronder in voorkomend geval versleuteling, teneinde de gevolgen van beveiligingsincidenten op gebruikers en op andere netwerken en diensten zo laag mogelijk te houden
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communication following a data or ICT security event, but they do not require the same practical compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a processor to promptly notify the controller after becoming aware of a personal-data breach. Norm B requires financial entities to maintain crisis-communication plans enabling responsible disclosure of serious ICT incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparties, and potentially the public. The former is an event-triggered notification duty between specific entities; the latter is a standing planning and preparedness obligation involving external communications.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: immediate bilateral notification versus maintaining a crisis-communication plan for possible broader disclosure.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken financiële entiteiten over crisiscommunicatieplannen die het mogelijk maken ten minste ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten of kwetsbaarheden op verantwoordelijke wijze bekend te maken aan cliënten en tegenpartijen en, in voorkomend geval, aan het publiek.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to make a substantive assessment or classification concerning a cyber/ICT threat or incident, but they do not require the same practical compliance act.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an entity, in an early warning sent to the CSIRT and competent authority, to state whether a significant incident was probably caused by an unlawful or malicious act (and, in the broader provision, also provide related information). Norm B requires a financial entity to classify cyber threats as significant using specified criteria concerning critical services, affected clients or counterparties, and geographic spread. The former is incident-cause reporting; the latter is threat-severity classification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required outputs and compliance purposes differ materially: reporting a suspected cause in an early-warning notification versus classifying a cyber threat as significant according to prescribed impact criteria.
verdict.evidence_span_a: geeft de entiteit aan of het significante incident vermoedelijk door een onrechtmatige of kwaadwillige handeling is veroorzaakt
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten classificeren cyberdreigingen als significant op basis van de mate waarin de risicovolle diensten, waaronder de transacties en verrichtingen van de financiële entiteit, als cruciaal kunnen worden aangemerkt, het aantal en/of de relevantie van de beoogde cliënten of financiële tegenpartijen en de geografische spreiding van de risicogebieden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to or managing digital-security risks, but they do not require the same operational compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an addressee to promptly notify the Minister and provide all necessary information about a security/integrity breach or misuse. Norm B requires a testing programme involving specified ICT-security and resilience tests, with risk-based planning and testing before certain deployments or redeployments; it is not a notification duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required acts differ in substance: immediate incident reporting and information disclosure versus conducting and planning technical/security assessments and tests.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening
verdict.evidence_span_b: voorziet, overeenkomstig de criteria in artikel 4, lid 2, in de uitvoering van passende tests, zoals kwetsbaarheidsbeoordelingen en -scans, opensourceanalyses, netwerkbeveiligingsbeoordelingen, kloofanalyses, beoordelingen van fysieke beveiliging, vragenlijsten en scanningsoftwareoplossingen, beoordelingen van broncodes indien mogelijk, scenariogebaseerde tests, compatibiliteitstests, prestatietests, eind-tot-eindtests en penetratietests

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communication/reporting in response to ICT or AI-related incidents and involve communicating externally to an identified audience or authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a financial entity to designate a person to implement its ICT-incident communication strategy and act as spokesperson to the public and media. Norm B requires reporting a serious incident involving specified high-risk AI systems to the designated national competent authority in the Member State where the incident occurred. These are different substantive actions, recipients, and compliance functions.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions are substantively different: public/media communications strategy and spokesperson duties versus a formal regulatory incident report to a competent authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: wordt belast met de uitvoering van de communicatiestrategie voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en vervult daartoe de rol van woordvoerder bij het publiek en de media
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms respond to a data-related event by requiring the regulated provider to take a protective/compliance measure, but the measures are materially different.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires prompt notification of the affected individual about a qualifying personal-data breach. Norm B requires data-reporting-service providers to maintain systems that check transaction reports for completeness, detect omissions and obvious errors, and request retransmission. One is an incident-notification duty; the other is an ongoing technical detection and correction capability.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: individual breach notification versus operating systems for transaction-report validation, error detection, and retransmission requests.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address protection against risks to personal/data security following or concerning a data-security incident, and both are relevant to entities handling digital data.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a conditional incident-notification duty: the controller must report a personal-data breach to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of it (unless unlikely to pose a risk), with reasons for delay. Norm B imposes an ongoing preventive ICT-security duty on financial entities to use suitable technologies and processes that prevent availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality, and data-loss failures. One is external regulatory notification after a breach; the other is preventive technical and organisational protection.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action differs in substance: mandatory breach reporting to a supervisory authority versus implementing preventive ICT safeguards.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: voorkomen een gebrek aan beschikbaarheid, de aantasting van de authenticiteit en integriteit, de inbreuken op de vertrouwelijkheid en het verlies van gegevens

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to establish and maintain an organizational cybersecurity/ICT-risk-management measure or framework intended to improve resilience against incidents and risks.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a broad, all-hazards cybersecurity risk-control approach comprising at least specified security policies and operational measures. Norm B specifically requires non-micro financial entities to establish, maintain, and evaluate a comprehensive, risk-based programme for testing digital operational resilience, including assessments, tests, methodologies, practices, and tools. The testing programme is a distinct assurance/testing obligation, not the same as implementing the underlying security controls.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: A mandates implementation of broad preventive and protective cybersecurity measures, whereas B mandates a recurring, comprehensive programme to test and evaluate digital operational resilience and identify deficiencies for corrective action.
verdict.evidence_span_a: zijn gebaseerd op een benadering die alle gevaren omvat en tot doel heeft netwerk- en informatiesystemen en de fysieke omgeving van die systemen tegen incidenten te beschermen, en omvatten ten minste het volgende
verdict.evidence_span_b: voor het vaststellen, handhaven en evalueren van een degelijk en alomvattend programma voor het testen van de digitale operationele weerbaarheid

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern communication or handling following a reported data/ICT incident, but they do not require the same practical compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes a concrete, prompt notification duty on a processor to inform the controller of a personal-data breach. Norm B states that financial entities remain fully responsible for handling and consequences of reported ICT incidents; it does not impose an equivalent notification duty on them.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required action, responsible actor, and operational object differ: prompt incident notification versus continued substantive responsibility for incident handling and consequences.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onverminderd de ontvangen feedback van toezichthouders blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms respond to an incident or breach by requiring the regulated entity to take a compliance-related step, but the required steps are not the same: Norm A requires reporting a significant incident to the CSIRT and competent authority, while Norm B requires maintaining an internal register of personal-data breaches.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external notification duty, with a 72-hour (or, for certain trust-service providers, 24-hour) deadline and specified incident information. Norm B is an ongoing record-keeping duty concerning all personal-data breaches; it does not require notification to the bodies named in Norm A.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actual compliance actions differ in substance: external incident notification versus internal maintenance of a breach register.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational handling of ICT/data incidents, but they require different operational measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires maintaining a register containing all personal-data breaches and specified factual information. Norm B requires assigning at least one person to implement the ICT-incident communications strategy and act as spokesperson to the public and media.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions are substantively different: record-keeping versus designation of a communications officer/spokesperson.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen leggen een verplichting op die verband houdt met het verstrekken of verwerken van informatie in een digitale-risicocontext.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A verplicht een brede groep organisaties om, op verzoek én uit eigen beweging, noodzakelijke gegevens en inlichtingen aan de minister te verstrekken zodat overheidsmaatregelen kunnen worden genomen. Norm B verplicht bepaalde financiële entiteiten intern operationele conclusies uit tests en incidentanalyses in hun ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces op te nemen; er is geen verstrekking aan een overheidsorgaan vereist.
verdict.criterion_fired: De feitelijke compliance-actie en geadresseerde verschillen wezenlijk: externe informatieverstrekking aan de minister versus interne verwerking van evaluatie-informatie binnen het ICT-risicobeheer.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern action following a legally relevant event, but they do not require the same practical compliance action. Norm A requires an entity to promptly notify its service recipients about significant incidents; Norm B concerns the lead overseer imposing a daily coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider, for up to six months after notifying the decision.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-notification duty owed to service recipients by an essential or important entity. Norm B is a supervisory enforcement measure involving the imposition of a coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party ICT-services provider.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required actions, actors, and legal functions differ substantively: recipient notification versus regulatory imposition of a coercive fine.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms respond to ICT/data-related risk by requiring action concerning that risk, but their practical compliance duties are not the same.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires prompt notification to the affected person of a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect privacy. Norm B requires financial entities to continuously identify ICT-risk sources and assess relevant cyber threats and vulnerabilities, with periodic risk-scenario evaluation. The former is an incident-notification duty; the latter is an ongoing risk-identification and assessment duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: affected-person breach notification versus continuous ICT-risk identification and vulnerability assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern actions triggered by an ICT/significant incident, but their required compliance actions are not substantially the same: Norm A requires promptly sending an early warning containing specified information to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority; Norm B requires internally classifying ICT-related incidents and assessing their effects using listed criteria.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external notification/reporting duty with a 24-hour deadline and specified recipients and content. Norm B is an internal incident-classification and impact-assessment duty, with no recipient or deadline stated.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative compliance action, recipient, and practical purpose differ materially: external early-warning notification versus internal classification and impact determination.
verdict.evidence_span_a: geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: classificeren ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en bepalen de effecten daarvan op basis van de volgende criteria

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating information about serious ICT/AI incidents to an external recipient. However, they do not require the same operational compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires financial entities to maintain crisis-communication plans enabling responsible disclosure to clients, counterparties, and potentially the public. Norm B requires high-risk AI providers to make an incident report to the competent market-surveillance authorities, immediately once causation or likely causation is established and subject to specific maximum deadlines, followed by investigation and cooperation duties.
verdict.criterion_fired: The recipient, purpose, and operational form of the duty differ materially: stakeholder/public crisis communication under A versus regulatory incident reporting and follow-up investigation under B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: beschikken financiële entiteiten over crisiscommunicatieplannen die het mogelijk maken ten minste ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten of kwetsbaarheden op verantwoordelijke wijze bekend te maken aan cliënten en tegenpartijen en, in voorkomend geval, aan het publiek
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms are triggered by a serious/significant ICT incident and impose an incident-related compliance action on the regulated entity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an urgent external early warning to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, within 24 hours where immediate notification is not possible, including specified incident and contact information. Norm B requires an internal post-incident evaluation: analyzing causes, assessing the response and procedures, and identifying improvements; certain entities must also communicate resulting changes to competent authorities on request. These are different substantive actions and recipients, despite the shared incident trigger.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: immediate incident notification versus post-incident investigation, evaluation, and remediation planning.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, analyseren daarbij de oorzaken van de verstoring en identificeren de verbeteringen die moeten worden aangebracht in de ICT-activiteiten of in het kader van het ICT-bedrijfscontinuïteitsbeleid als bedoeld in artikel 11.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to a triggering incident involving the regulated subject, but they do not require the same operational act: Norm A requires internal documentation of personal-data breaches, whereas Norm B requires prompt external notification of serious AI incidents to market-surveillance authorities, followed by investigation and cooperation procedures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a recordkeeping/documentation duty concerning all personal-data breaches and their facts, consequences, and corrective measures. Norm B is an authority-notification duty concerning serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems, with specified recipients and deadlines; its related provisions also require investigation, risk assessment, corrective measures, and cooperation after notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The core compliance actions are substantively different: documenting an incident for supervisory-verification purposes versus reporting an incident to designated market-surveillance authorities within a prescribed timeframe.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen reageren op een ICT-/AI-incident, maar vereisen verschillende soorten nalevingshandelingen: Norm A vereist interne classificatie en effectbeoordeling aan de hand van criteria; Norm B vereist externe melding van een ernstig incident binnen een bepaalde termijn.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een inhoudelijke interne beoordelings- en classificatieplicht. Norm B is een procedurele meldingsplicht, met onmiddellijke melding zodra het causale verband is vastgesteld of vermoed en uiterlijk binnen tien dagen na bewustwording van het incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: De feitelijke compliance-actie verschilt substantieel: classificeren en effecten bepalen versus een ernstig incident melden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the relevant provider to notify a public authority of a qualifying security/significant incident without delay.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a trust-service provider to report a significant incident affecting its trust service to both its CSIRT and competent authority, within 24 hours if immediate reporting is impossible, with the fuller report content specified in the referenced paragraph. Norm B requires a public electronic communications service provider to notify only the Dutch Data Protection Authority of a security breach having adverse effects on the protection of processed personal data, with no 24-hour fallback or equivalent specified content in the provision.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required recipients and substantive incident/reporting scope differ: A is a cybersecurity incident report to two bodies concerning continuity/effects on a trust service, while B is a personal-data security-breach notification to the data-protection authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to create and maintain documentation concerning a specified subject: personal-data breaches under Norm A, and the ICT risk-management framework under Norm B.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires documenting every personal-data breach, including its facts, consequences, and corrective measures, so that the supervisory authority can verify compliance. Norm B requires periodic and incident-triggered documentation and evaluation of an ICT risk-management framework, continuous improvement based on implementation and monitoring lessons, and submission of an evaluation report upon request. The objects, triggers, and substantive activities therefore differ.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms share a documentation-related action and a broadly similar addressee category, but they do not impose substantially the same practical compliance duty: one is breach-record documentation, while the other is recurring evaluation and improvement of an ICT risk-management framework, with possible reporting.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern post-incident compliance, but they require materially different actions: Norm A requires submitting a formal final (or, where applicable, interim) incident report to specified authorities, while Norm B requires incorporating operational lessons from testing and post-incident analysis into the entity’s internal ICT-risk-assessment process.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external reporting and information-submission duty with a deadline and prescribed incident-content requirements. Norm B is an ongoing internal risk-management and learning duty, with no submission to a regulator or other recipient and no incident-report deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: external incident reporting versus internal incorporation of lessons into risk assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms respond to a risk-related event by requiring protective or remedial compliance measures, but they do not require the same practical action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires financial entities to implement ICT safeguards that prevent or reduce data-security failures, including loss of availability, compromised authenticity or integrity, confidentiality breaches, and data loss. Norm B requires the provider or potential provider to report each serious incident occurring during real-world testing to the national market-surveillance authority; the provision also requires immediate mitigation, suspension, or termination of testing and a recall procedure.
verdict.criterion_fired: The operative compliance actions differ in substance: ongoing preventive ICT security controls versus incident notification to a regulator (with associated testing-continuation and recall measures).

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to submit a report/notification concerning a serious incident to the relevant authority or recipient within a specified time after becoming aware of, or reporting, the incident.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a substantive final (or, where the incident continues, interim) report to both the CSIRT and competent authority, containing a detailed description, cause/threat, mitigation measures, and possible cross-border effects. Norm B requires an incident notification triggered by death and a suspected or established causal link to a high-risk AI system, with a specific ten-day outer deadline; it does not impose the same detailed final-report contents or dual-recipient submission.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action differs in substance: A is a detailed post-incident final/progress reporting duty, whereas B is a prompt serious-incident notification duty triggered by a fatality and causal-link assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern legal consequences or reporting related to unlawful/significant data-processing or cybersecurity incidents, but they do not require the same practical compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes substantive civil liability for damage caused by GDPR-infringing processing (or processor-specific breaches/mis instructions). verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires non-micro financial entities to establish, maintain, and evaluate a comprehensive digital operational-resilience testing programme, implemented on a risk-based basis. Norm B requires specified entities to submit ICT-incident notifications, including voluntary notifications, to the designated sectoral CSIRT in addition to any other required recipient.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve post-incident or incident-related compliance activity concerning ICT/AI risks, but they do not require the same practical action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires financial entities to conduct post-incident evaluations after serious ICT-related disruptions, analyze causes, assess the effectiveness of procedures and measures, and identify improvements. Norm B requires providers of systemically risky general-purpose AI models to maintain and document information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures and report it without delay to specified authorities.

Norm B requires the controller to notify the affected data subject of a high-risk personal-data breach, subject to specified exceptions or substitute public communication.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een doorlopende preventieve/detectieve capaciteitsverplichting voor financiële entiteiten. Norm B is een concrete meldingsverplichting na een ernstig incident, gericht aan een nationale autoriteit.

Norm B requires notifying a market-surveillance authority of the results of a fundamental-rights impact assessment and submitting a completed template; it is an external regulatory notification tied to the assessment, not incident management or recordkeeping.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: internal incident registration and management versus external notification of an AI fundamental-rights assessment with a completed template.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to take action in response to an incident or operational-resilience concern, but the required actions are not substantially the same.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires establishing, maintaining, and evaluating a comprehensive digital-operational-resilience testing programme, including risk-based testing activities. Norm B requires an immediate investigation of a serious incident and the AI system, including incident risk assessment and corrective measures, with cooperation and safeguards against compromising the investigation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The core compliance actions differ in substance: an ongoing, structured testing-programme obligation versus an urgent, incident-specific investigation obligation.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to report a serious incident to a public authority: DORA requires financial entities to submit serious ICT-related-incident notifications and reports to the relevant competent authority, while the AI Act requires providers of high-risk AI systems to report serious incidents to the relevant market-surveillance authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ in substance because they apply to different regulated activities and require reporting to different authorities, with materially different reporting schemes. DORA entails a structured sequence of initial, interim/updated, and final reports under Article 19(4), using prescribed models and containing information enabling assessment of scope and cross-border effects. The AI Act duty is a serious-incident notification by high-risk-AI providers to the market-surveillance authority, with the cited paragraph chiefly imposing an immediate and, for widespread breaches or serious incidents, two-day deadline. The shared incident-reporting concept is not enough to make the compliance action substantially identical.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different substantive reporting regimes: different regulated subjects and recipient authorities, and DORA requires a multi-stage, model-based incident-reporting package rather than merely the AI Act's serious-incident notification within the specified deadline.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen verplichten een aangewezen organisatie om informatie aan een overheids- of toezichthoudende instantie te verstrekken naar aanleiding van een vooraf bepaalde gebeurtenis of beoordeling.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A vereist een snelle incidentmelding aan zowel het CSIRT als de bevoegde autoriteit, met incidentinformatie en eventuele updates/beoordelingen. Norm B vereist daarentegen kennisgeving aan de markttoezichtautoriteit van de resultaten van een vooraf uitgevoerde grondrechteneffectbeoordeling, inclusief een ingevuld sjabloon; het gaat niet om incidentrapportage.
verdict.criterion_fired: De concrete compliance-acties verschillen materieel: incidentmelding met operationele incidentgegevens aan twee ontvangers versus rapportage van de resultaten van een grondrechtenbeoordeling met een voorgeschreven formulier aan één markttoezichtautoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Na een incident een melding/informatie verstrekken aan een externe ontvanger zonder onredelijke vertraging.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A vereist onverwijlde kennisgeving aan de ontvangers van de eigen diensten over significante incidenten die hun dienstverlening nadelig kunnen beïnvloeden. Norm B vereist melding aan de bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, in beginsel uiterlijk binnen 72 uur na kennisneming, met een motivering bij vertraging en een risico-uitzondering.
verdict.criterion_fired: De verplichte ontvanger en het materiële doel van de handeling verschillen wezenlijk: dienstontvangers informeren over dienstverstorende significante incidenten versus een privacy-inbreuk melden aan de toezichthouder voor toezicht/doeleinden van gegevensbescherming.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten
verdict.evidence_span_b: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the addressee to submit a report or notification concerning an incident to a competent public body, within a specified time after becoming aware of or handling the incident.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns a substitute progress report when an incident is still ongoing, followed by a final report within one month after the incident is handled, including detailed incident, cause, mitigation, and possible cross-border-impact information. Norm B concerns an immediate serious-incident notification to market-surveillance authorities, with a maximum deadline of two days after awareness; it is a regulatory incident notification rather than a progress/final report regime.
verdict.criterion_fired: The obligations differ substantively in the required submission: A requires a progress report replacing a due final report and later a comprehensive final report, whereas B requires an immediate serious-incident notification to market-surveillance authorities within two days of awareness.

verdict.evidence_span_b: de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an organisational measure addressing ICT/cybersecurity risks, but their concrete compliance actions are not the same.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a comprehensive, risk-based cybersecurity framework containing multiple specified technical, organisational, continuity, supply-chain, personnel, and authentication measures. Norm B requires appointing at least one person to implement the ICT-incident communications strategy and act as spokesperson to the public and media.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required operational action differs in substance: broad implementation of an all-hazards cybersecurity control programme versus designation of a communications officer/spokesperson for ICT incidents.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require prompt reporting or communication of an incident to an external recipient after the responsible entity becomes aware of it.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the controller to communicate a personal-data breach directly to the affected data subject where it is likely to create a high risk. Norm B requires incident reporting by covered entities to the CSIRT or competent authority, with multiple staged reports, specified content, and deadlines (including a 24-hour deadline for trust-service providers). The recipients, incident types, and reporting functions therefore differ substantially.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance action is substantively different because the norms impose communications to different recipients for different purposes: individual notification of affected persons versus regulatory/CSIRT incident reporting with structured follow-up reports.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms respond to security-related incidents or risks, but they do not require the same operational act: Norm A requires implementing ongoing technical, operational, and organisational security measures, whereas Norm B requires submitting a serious-incident notification to market-surveillance authorities within a specified deadline.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive risk-management and security-control obligation for providers of public electronic communications services. Norm B is a reactive reporting obligation for providers of high-risk AI systems, triggered by awareness of a serious incident and directed to Member State market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: implementing security safeguards versus notifying authorities of an incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational responses to cyber-related events, but they do not require the same practical compliance action. Norm A requires an entity to promptly inform potentially affected service recipients about measures they can take, and where necessary about the significant cyber threat itself. Norm B requires financial entities to register ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats and to establish procedures for monitoring, handling, follow-up, and root-cause remediation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external communication and warning duty directed at potentially affected service recipients. Norm B is an internal incident-recording and incident-management-process duty; it does not require notifying recipients.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions differ in substance: recipient-facing threat communication versus internal registration and management of incidents and threats.
verdict.evidence_span_a: deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms are triggered in the context of a cybersecurity or data-related incident/threat, but they do not require the same operational compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a processor to notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal-data breach. Norm B requires financial entities to classify cyber threats as significant using specified impact and exposure criteria; it does not require notification to another party.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required action differs in substance: external/internal notification versus classification and assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het voorkomen of beëindigen van beveiligingsincidenten en aantasting van digitale betrouwbaarheid, maar zij leggen niet dezelfde concrete handeling op.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A verplicht aangewezen bestuursorganen en andere genoemde partijen om op verzoek of uit eigen beweging noodzakelijke gegevens en inlichtingen aan de minister te verstrekken. Norm B verplicht financiële entiteiten om passende ICT-technologieën en -processen te gebruiken die gegevensbeschermings- en beschikbaarheidsrisico’s voorkomen; het is een materiële ICT-beveiligingsverplichting, geen informatieverstrekking aan een autoriteit.
verdict.criterion_fired: De vereiste compliance-acties verschillen wezenlijk: informatie aan de minister verstrekken versus passende ICT-beveiligingsmaatregelen implementeren en gebruiken.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve providing information to a public authority, but their substantive compliance duties differ.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires broad, on-demand and proactive provision of data and information needed by the Minister to prevent or end infringements affecting secure and reliable electronic access. Norm B requires certain financial entities, upon request, to report changes implemented after ICT-related post-incident evaluations; those evaluations concern causes, improvements, procedural compliance, and effectiveness of measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required information, purpose, and underlying duty differ materially: general regulatory information assistance in Norm A versus post-incident remediation-change reporting in Norm B.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern an entity responding to cybersecurity-related risks or incidents, but they do not require the same practical compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to send a prompt early warning about a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority, including specified information and contact details. Norm B requires a financial entity to maintain capabilities and personnel resources to collect information about vulnerabilities, cyber threats, and ICT incidents and analyze their likely effects on digital operational resilience. The former is an incident-notification duty; the latter is an ongoing organizational capability and analysis duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required acts, recipients, and temporal character differ substantially: external notification within 24 hours versus maintaining internal resources and capabilities for information gathering and analysis.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern organizational responses to cybersecurity/AI-related risks or incidents, but they require different operational measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires financial entities to maintain capabilities and personnel to collect and analyze information about vulnerabilities, threats, and incidents. Norm B requires reporting each serious incident to the national market-surveillance authority and taking immediate mitigation, suspension, termination, and recall-procedure measures during real-world testing.
verdict.criterion_fired: The required compliance actions are substantively different: ongoing internal capability and resource provision versus incident notification and immediate corrective/testing measures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: beschikken over capaciteiten en personele middelen om informatie te verzamelen over kwetsbaarheden en cyberdreigingen, ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, met name cyberaanvallen, en om de waarschijnlijke gevolgen ervan voor hun digitale operationele weerbaarheid te analyseren

Norm B requires financial entities to register ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats and, additionally, to establish procedures and processes for monitoring, handling, follow-up, and remediation of root causes.
verdict.criterion_fired: The recording obligation is similar, but Norm B imposes a materially broader incident-management framework and covers a different incident category and regulated sector; the duties are not substantially the same in practice.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to problems affecting electronically transmitted or processed information, but they do not require the same compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the electronic communications service provider to notify the Dutch Data Protection Authority without delay about a qualifying personal-data security breach. Norm B requires data-reporting service providers to maintain systems that check transaction reports for completeness, detect omissions and obvious errors, and request retransmission. The former is an incident-reporting duty to a regulator; the latter is an ongoing technical monitoring and correction capability concerning transaction reports.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated entity to take measures addressing cybersecurity risks affecting data and ICT operations.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires a specific incident-reporting action: submitting a final (or, while the incident continues, progress) report to the CSIRT and competent authority, with prescribed incident details and deadlines. Norm B requires an ongoing preventive/technical control action: using suitable ICT technologies and processes to prevent availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality, and data-loss failures. These are different compliance obligations in substance.
