verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the responsible actor to communicate information to a public authority, but A requires urgent notification of a security/integrity breach or misuse of access, while B requires notification of the results of a fundamental-rights impact assessment and submission of a completed template before use of certain high-risk AI systems.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The triggering event and substantive information differ: A concerns an electronic-service security or access-misuse incident; B concerns completion of a fundamental-rights impact assessment for a high-risk AI system.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different event families and different actor roles: an electronic-service security/integrity incident or access misuse versus completion of a high-risk-AI fundamental-rights assessment.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening. Het bestuursorgaan of de aangewezen organisatie verstrekt daarbij alle benodigde informatie.
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to include specified information in an early warning about a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority; Norm B requires financial entities, during recovery from an ICT-related incident, to perform controls and reconciliations to preserve data integrity and consistency.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-warning/reporting content duty, including whether the incident was likely caused by an unlawful or malicious act, whether it may have cross-border effects, and the responsible reporting officer’s contact details. Norm B is an operational recovery and data-integrity control duty, not a reporting duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action and actor role: A concerns early-warning reporting by essential/important entities, while B concerns recovery controls by financial entities; the shared incident context does not make the compliance work duplicative.
verdict.evidence_span_a: geeft de entiteit aan of het significante incident vermoedelijk door een onrechtmatige of kwaadwillige handeling is veroorzaakt
verdict.evidence_span_b: verrichten financiële entiteiten de benodigde controles, ook meerdere controles, waaronder afstemmingen, om ervoor te zorgen dat het hoogste niveau van gegevensintegriteit wordt gehandhaafd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to include specified incident details and the responsible officer’s contact details in an early warning about a significant incident sent to its CSIRT and competent authority. Norm B requires data-reporting-service providers to operate systems that check transaction reports for completeness, detect omissions and obvious errors, and request retransmission.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-notification content duty triggered by a significant incident; Norm B is an ongoing technical control and retransmission-request duty concerning transaction reports.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering context, and operative action: incident warning/reporting versus maintaining systems for validating transaction reports and requesting retransmission.
verdict.evidence_span_a: geeft de entiteit aan of het significante incident vermoedelijk door een onrechtmatige of kwaadwillige handeling is veroorzaakt
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern handling information about an incident: informing service recipients of significant incidents under Norm A, versus documenting personal-data breaches and their facts, consequences, and corrective measures under Norm B.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires prompt notification to the entity’s service recipients; Norm B requires the controller to document every personal-data breach so the supervisory authority can assess compliance. The duties differ in actor role, recipient/purpose, and substantive content.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying duties are not the same: Norm A is an urgent outward notification to service recipients about significant service-affecting incidents, while Norm B is internal documentation of personal-data breaches for supervisory compliance control. The different actor role and low content overlap make this more than an additional-recipient duplicate.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten
verdict.evidence_span_b: documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen raken aan het reageren op ICT-/AI-gerelateerde incidenten, maar norm A verplicht tot het opzetten en onderhouden van detectie- en incidentafhandelingscapaciteit; norm B verplicht tot het daadwerkelijk melden van een ernstig incident.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een doorlopende organisatorische en technische beheersmaatregel zonder meldplicht of aangewezen ontvanger. Norm B is een concrete meldplicht voor een ernstig incident met overlijden, gericht aan de bevoegde autoriteit(en), met een uiterste termijn van tien dagen na bewustwording.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie en de actorrol verschillen: A betreft doorlopende ICT-risicobeheersing en incidentdetectie/-afhandeling door bepaalde financiële entiteiten; B betreft melding van een ernstig AI-incident door een aanbieder of gebruiksverantwoordelijke. De gedeelde incidentcontext maakt de verplichtingen niet tot dezelfde compliance-werkzaamheden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: ervoor zorgen dat bronnen van ICT-risico’s en anomalieën in de netwerk- en informatiesystemen zo spoedig mogelijk worden geïdentificeerd en gedetecteerd en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten snel kunnen worden afgehandeld
verdict.evidence_span_b: bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an essential or important entity to use only products or services other than those identified by the Minister; B requires specified actors to provide the Minister with data and information, on request or voluntarily, for measures concerning secure and reliable access to electronic services.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms address different compliance actions and different subject matters: procurement/use restrictions based on national-security supplier risk versus information provision concerning electronic-service access.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action, triggering regulatory concern, and actor role differ; any superficial similarity from ministerial involvement does not create the same reporting or compliance duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: legt hij in overeenstemming met Onze Minister een essentiële entiteit of een belangrijke entiteit de verplichting op om in de daarbij aangewezen onderdelen van haar netwerk- en informatiesystemen uitsluitend gebruik te maken van producten of diensten van anderen dan de daarbij door Onze Minister die het aangaat genoemde partij
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft om maatregelen te kunnen nemen om inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening te voorkomen of beëindigen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/cyber-risk handling by financial-sector entities, but A requires classification of cyber threats as significant, whereas B requires making an ICT-incident notification to the designated sectoral CSIRT (including voluntary notifications) in addition to the notification under DORA Article 19.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an internal classification/assessment duty concerning the significance of cyber threats; Norm B is an external incident-reporting duty to a CSIRT. The texts do not impose the same verb-level action or require the same substantive output.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad cyber/ICT-risk event family and financial-entity actor role, but classification and incident notification are distinct compliance actions with materially different content and purposes; the additional CSIRT recipient does not itself make the duties different, but the underlying work is not identical.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten classificeren cyberdreigingen als significant
verdict.evidence_span_b: doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A imposes civil liability for damage caused by processing that infringes the GDPR; B requires certain financial entities to establish, maintain, and evaluate a comprehensive digital-operational-resilience testing programme, using a risk-based approach and specified testing activities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is a liability consequence tied to unlawful processing and resulting damage, whereas B is a proactive ICT-resilience governance and testing obligation; neither requires the same compliance work.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor scope, operative action, and subject matter: GDPR damage liability for infringing processing versus establishment, maintenance, and evaluation of an ICT-resilience testing programme.
verdict.evidence_span_a: is aansprakelijk voor de schade die wordt veroorzaakt door verwerking die inbreuk maakt op deze verordening
verdict.evidence_span_b: voor het vaststellen, handhaven en evalueren van een degelijk en alomvattend programma voor het testen van de digitale operationele weerbaarheid

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/security-related compliance, but A requires urgent notification of a security or access-abuse incident with all necessary information, whereas B requires periodic and incident-triggered documentation and evaluation of an ICT-risk-management framework, plus submission of an evaluation report on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident notification duty to the Minister; Norm B is an internal ICT-risk-management documentation/evaluation duty, with a report submitted to the competent authority only upon request.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action and duty-bearing role differ: A requires an administrative body or designated organisation to notify the Minister immediately about a security/integrity breach or access misuse, while B requires a financial entity to document and evaluate its ICT-risk-management framework periodically and after serious ICT-related incidents. The shared ICT/security context is insufficient to establish the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve an actor communicating information to a public authority, but A requires reporting every significant incident, whereas B requires supplying data and information needed by the Minister, on request or proactively, to prevent or end interference with secure and reliable access to electronic services.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty for essential or important entities; Norm B is a broader information-supply/cooperation duty imposed on several categories of organisations for a preventive or remedial governmental purpose.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering event, actor scope, and required content/purpose; the superficial similarity of communicating information to a public authority is insufficient.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, op grond van artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houders van een erkenning en op grond van artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgevers en diensten verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft om maatregelen te kunnen nemen om inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening te voorkomen of beëindigen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern maintaining or providing information connected with incidents, but they require different compliance actions: A requires keeping an internal register of all personal-data breaches; B requires supplying competent authorities, on request, with an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing internal record-keeping duty covering all personal-data breaches and specified facts/data; Norm B is an on-request disclosure to competent authorities by financial entities, limited to an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action and actor role differ, and the required content and purpose substantially differ; the shared incident-related context is insufficient to make this duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: houdt een overzicht bij van alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires data-reporting-service providers to operate systems that check transaction reports for completeness, detect omissions and obvious errors, and request retransmission. B requires conformity-assessment bodies to submit an application for notification to the competent notifying authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different actors, different event families, and fundamentally different actions: operational validation and retransmission requests versus an application for designation/notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different core duty/event family; the apparent similarity does not establish overlapping compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern handling ICT/security-related events, but A requires an entity to issue an early warning to its CSIRT and competent authority, whereas B requires a financial entity to maintain and regularly test detection mechanisms for anomalous activities, ICT incidents, network-performance issues, and physical single points of failure.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-triggered external notification duty with specified warning content and a 24-hour deadline; Norm B is an ongoing internal capability, detection, and testing duty, with no reporting recipient.
verdict.criterion_fired: The core actions and actor roles differ: A requires an essential or important entity to notify designated incident-response authorities about a significant incident, while B requires a financial entity to operate and test detection mechanisms. The shared ICT/security context is insufficient to create duplicate compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten beschikken over mechanismen om overeenkomstig artikel 17 afwijkende activiteiten zo spoedig mogelijk te detecteren, met inbegrip van kwesties op het gebied van ICT-netwerkprestaties en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, en om potentiële zwakke fysieke punten (“single points of failure”) te identificeren.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to ICT/cyber incidents, but A requires urgent communication to potentially affected service recipients about protective measures (and, if necessary, the threat), whereas B requires financial entities to establish and implement an internal ICT-incident management process covering detection, handling, classification, escalation, communication planning, and response.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external, event-triggered information duty to service recipients; Norm B is an ongoing organisational/process duty imposed on financial entities, not a specific report or notification to the recipients identified in A.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action and actor role: A requires an essential or important entity to promptly inform potentially affected service recipients, while B requires financial entities to design, adopt, and implement an ICT-incident management process. The shared incident-related subject matter is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern addressing consequences or risks associated with security/ICT incidents, but A requires preventive technical, operational, and organisational risk-management measures, whereas B requires financial entities to provide competent authorities, on request, with an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes an ongoing preventive security-risk management obligation on providers of public electronic communications networks or services; Norm B imposes an on-request information-provision obligation on non-micro financial entities concerning quantified annual incident costs and losses.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different verb-level duty: implementing security measures versus providing a cost-and-loss estimate on request. The shared incident-related context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde meldingsplicht: norm A verplicht het opnemen van operationele conclusies uit tests en incidentanalyse in het interne ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces; norm B verplicht het melden van ernstige AI-incidenten aan markttoezichtautoriteiten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een interne governance- en risicobeoordelingsmaatregel zonder ontvanger of termijn; norm B is een externe melding aan markttoezichtautoriteiten met een termijn van onmiddellijk en uiterlijk 15 dagen, met kortere termijnen voor bepaalde gevallen.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie en actorrol verschillen: A betreft interne verwerking van conclusies uit ICT-risicotests en incidentanalyse door bepaalde financiële entiteiten; B betreft melding van ernstige AI-incidenten door aanbieders of gebruiksverantwoordelijken aan markttoezichtautoriteiten. Een gedeelde incidentcontext maakt de verplichtingen slechts verwant, niet duplicatief.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de relevante operationele conclusies die voortvloeien uit de in punt g) bedoelde tests en uit de analyse na een incident opnemen in het ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an entity to report incident-related information promptly to competent public-sector recipients, but they do not require the same report or the same underlying compliance work.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an early warning about a significant incident, including whether it was likely caused by an unlawful or malicious act, possible cross-border effects, and the responsible reporting officer’s contact details. Norm B requires keeping and documenting relevant information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures, then reporting it to the AI Office and, where applicable, national competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not meaningfully the same because they apply to different actor roles and require materially different incident information and purposes: NIS2-type essential or important entities must issue an early warning about a significant incident, whereas providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk must maintain, document, and report information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/significant-incident reporting or follow-up, but Norm A imposes an incident-notification duty on an entity, while Norm B describes supervisory feedback and preserves the financial entity’s responsibility for incidents already reported under Article 19(1). Norm B does not impose the same reporting action on the financial entity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires the entity to submit a significant-incident notification to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours (with the fuller Article 27 reporting content and an initial assessment framework). Norm B concerns what the competent authority may do after receiving an Article 19(4) notification/reports and states that the financial entity remains responsible for handling and consequences; it does not require that entity to make the Article 27 notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not have the same actor bearing the same verb-level obligation: A requires an essential/important trust-service entity to report an incident; B assigns post-notification feedback/oversight functions to the competent authority and states continuing responsibility of financial entities, without imposing a duplicate report.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: bevestigt de bevoegde autoriteit na ontvangst van de in artikel 19, lid 4, bedoelde eerste kennisgeving en verslagen, de ontvangst ervan en kan zij, waar mogelijk, tijdig relevante en evenredige feedback of richtsnoeren op hoog niveau aan de financiële entiteit verstrekken

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires maintaining a register/overview of all personal-data breaches, including specified facts and data. Both concern incident-related governance, but B is an operational management framework rather than the same record-keeping duty.

The texts do not establish that B requires maintaining the same overview or reporting the same information.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in their core action and actor scope: A requires a public electronic communications service provider to keep a register of personal-data breaches, while B requires financial entities to implement an ICT-incident management process. The shared incident-related subject matter is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address protection against security-related threats or incidents affecting secure electronic communications/services, but Norm A requires supplying information to the Minister, while Norm B requires implementing technical, operational, and organisational security measures.

verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and duty-bearing actor categories differ: Norm A requires providing information to a Minister, whereas Norm B requires communications providers to implement security measures. The shared security-incident/security-access context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating information to a public authority in connection with a potentially harmful or problematic situation, but Norm A requires supplying information needed by the Minister to prevent or end breaches affecting secure and reliable electronic access, whereas Norm B requires reporting every serious incident identified during real-world testing and also entails immediate risk mitigation, suspension, termination, and recall procedures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a broad, request-based or proactive information-supply duty concerning breaches of secure electronic access; Norm B is a specific serious-incident reporting duty tied to real-world testing of high-risk AI systems, coupled with immediate operational safety measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not concern the same event family or the same actor role: Norm A applies to specified public bodies, organisations, recognised holders, issuers and service providers in relation to secure electronic access, while Norm B applies to an AI provider or potential provider during real-world testing and concerns serious incidents. The reporting verbs and public-authority recipients are not enough to establish duplicated compliance work.

Norm B requires providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk to keep and document relevant information on serious incidents and possible corrective measures, and report it without delay to the AI Office and, where applicable, national competent authorities.

Norm B is an incident-information retention, documentation, and urgent reporting duty for systemic-risk general-purpose AI-model providers, directed to authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling ICT/AI-related incidents, but Norm A requires financial entities to classify an ICT-related incident and assess its effects, whereas Norm B requires reporting a serious incident to the national market-surveillance authority and taking immediate risk-mitigation, suspension, termination, and recall-procedure measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an internal incident-classification and impact-assessment duty for financial entities; Norm B is an external serious-incident reporting and immediate risk-response duty for providers or potential providers testing high-risk AI in real-world conditions.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both the core action and actor role: Norm A requires financial entities to classify and assess ICT incidents, while Norm B requires an AI provider or potential provider to report a serious testing incident and take risk-control measures. verdict.criterion_fired: The event family overlaps, but the actor roles, recipients, and core duties differ: Norm A concerns the contents of notifications by the provider to the authority and affected person, whereas Norm B concerns a processor informing the controller.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve reporting an incident to a public authority, but Norm A requires a detailed final (or, where applicable, progress) report containing specified incident, cause, impact, and mitigation information, while Norm B requires reporting a serious incident during real-world testing under the procedure in Article 73; Norm B also separately requires immediate mitigation, suspension, or termination measures and a recall procedure.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling incidents through an incident-related compliance process, but Norm A requires notifying the competent supervisory authority of a personal-data breach, while Norm B requires financial entities to register ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats and establish procedures for monitoring, treatment, follow-up, and remediation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external, time-limited notification duty to a supervisory authority concerning a personal-data breach; Norm B is an internal registration and incident-management/process-establishment duty covering ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad incident-management context and actor role, but the operative actions, recipients, purposes, and required content differ: external breach notification under Norm A versus internal registration and establishment of ICT-incident management procedures under Norm B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen. Financiële entiteiten stellen passende procedures en processen vast voor een consistente en geïntegreerde monitoring, behandeling en follow-up van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern obligations arising in connection with an incident, but Norm A requires maintaining an internal register of personal-data breaches, whereas Norm B requires reporting serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems to market-surveillance authorities, followed by investigation and corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing record-keeping duty concerning all personal-data breaches; Norm B is an incident-notification duty concerning serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems, with specified authorities and deadlines.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad incident-related event family and broadly comparable provider role, but the operative actions and required content differ: internal retention of a breach overview versus external notification of serious AI incidents to market-surveillance authorities. The different recipient does not itself defeat duplication, but the low content overlap does.
verdict.evidence_span_a: houdt een overzicht bij van alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require an organization to promptly communicate information about a security-related incident or misuse event to a public-sector recipient. However, A is an early warning forming part of a broader significant-incident report and must include specified incident-causation, cross-border-impact, and contact information; B is an immediate notification of a breach or misuse involving the organization’s own electronic service, with all necessary information.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns an essential or important entity’s early warning about a significant incident to both its CSIRT and competent authority, within 24 hours where immediate notification is not possible. Norm B concerns a public body or designated organization notifying the Minister of a breach, integrity incident, or misuse of access to its own electronic service, without a fixed numerical deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor roles are materially different: A applies to essential or important entities under the NIS-style incident-reporting regime, while B applies to a bestuursorgaan or designated organization. The duties also address different incident scopes and reporting purposes, despite both involving prompt security-related incident notification to an authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require organizational cybersecurity measures concerning protection or monitoring against ICT/security incidents, but A imposes a broad, risk-based protective-measures framework while B requires deployment of resources and capabilities for operational monitoring and detection.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires implementing a comprehensive set of preventive, responsive, continuity, supply-chain, personnel, cryptographic and related cybersecurity measures; Norm B specifically requires monitoring user activity and ICT anomalies/incidents, especially cyberattacks.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same general cybersecurity-incident family and actor role, but the operative duties differ: broad risk-based protection and incident-handling measures versus specific monitoring and detection capabilities. The overlap is not the same compliance work repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De maatregelen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, zijn gebaseerd op een benadering die alle gevaren omvat en tot doel heeft netwerk- en informatiesystemen en de fysieke omgeving van die systemen tegen incidenten te beschermen
verdict.evidence_span_b: zetten voldoende middelen en capaciteiten in om toezicht te houden op activiteiten van gebruikers en het optreden van ICT-anomalieën en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires designated actors to provide the Minister, on request and proactively, data and information needed to prevent or end breaches affecting secure and reliable access to electronic services. Norm B concerns the lead overseer imposing a daily coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider until obligations are fulfilled, for up to six months after notification of the decision.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an information-provision duty imposed on specified organizations and other actors; Norm B is an enforcement measure imposed by the lead overseer, not a reporting or information duty borne by the same actor.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event context, and actor role: information provision to a Minister versus imposition of a coercive fine by a lead overseer.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 6 bedoelde dwangsom wordt dagelijks opgelegd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a controller to promptly communicate a high-risk personal-data breach to the affected data subject; B requires a financial entity to classify cyber threats as significant using specified risk, client/counterparty, and geographic criteria.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent breach notification to the data subject, whereas Norm B is an internal classification and significance-assessment measure for cyber threats, with no recipient or deadline specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A imposes breach communication by a data controller to a data subject, while B imposes cyber-threat classification by a financial entity. The shared incident/cyber-risk context is insufficient for duplicate burden, and B does not require the same notification work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: deelt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke de betrokkene de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens onverwijld mee
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten classificeren cyberdreigingen als significant

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A geeft een benadeelde persoon een recht op schadevergoeding na schade door een AVG-inbreuk; norm B verplicht financiële entiteiten preventieve ICT-beveiligingsmaatregelen te gebruiken.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een individueel schadevergoedingsrecht en aansprakelijkheid achteraf; norm B betreft preventieve beveiliging en risicobeperking door financiële entiteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: Verschillende kernactie, gebeurtenisfamilie en actorrol: schadevergoeding ontvangen versus preventieve ICT-beveiliging implementeren.
verdict.evidence_span_a: heeft het recht om van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker schadevergoeding te ontvangen voor de geleden schade
verdict.evidence_span_b: maken financiële entiteiten gebruik van ICT-technologieën en -processen die geschikt zijn overeenkomstig artikel 4

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT-incident-related compliance by financial-sector entities, but A requires internal data-integrity controls during recovery/reconstruction, whereas B requires making an ICT-incident report, including a voluntary report, to the designated sectoral CSIRT.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an internal recovery and data-integrity control duty; Norm B is an external incident-reporting duty to a CSIRT, additionally to the reporting arrangements referenced in Article 19.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and compliance purposes differ materially: A requires performing controls and reconciliations during ICT-incident recovery or data reconstruction, while B requires submitting an ICT-incident notification to a designated CSIRT. The shared ICT-incident context and financial-entity addressees do not make the duties duplicated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verrichten financiële entiteiten de benodigde controles, ook meerdere controles, waaronder afstemmingen, om ervoor te zorgen dat het hoogste niveau van gegevensintegriteit wordt gehandhaafd
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require informing or making a report after awareness of an adverse incident. However, Norm A requires a processor to inform the controller of a personal-data breach, while Norm B requires reporting a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system, specifically where a person has died and a causal link is established or suspected.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns a personal-data breach and an internal processor-to-controller notification without unreasonable delay. Norm B concerns a serious high-risk-AI incident involving death, requires reporting after a causal link is established or suspected, and imposes a maximum deadline of ten days (with the related paragraph providing the general 15-day rule).
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not the same because the actor role differs: Norm A is imposed on a processor notifying the controller, whereas Norm B is imposed on an AI provider or, where applicable, deployer/user responsible for reporting a serious high-risk-AI incident. The triggering incidents and required report content also differ materially.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A imposes liability for damage caused by processing that breaches the GDPR; B requires financial entities to perform controls and reconciliations during ICT-incident recovery or reconstruction to maintain data integrity. Both concern consequences or handling of problematic data/ICT events, but they require fundamentally different actions.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a liability rule allocating responsibility for compensating damage caused by unlawful processing; Norm B is an operational recovery and data-integrity control obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying duties, triggering circumstances, and responsible actor roles are materially different: A concerns liability for unlawful personal-data processing, while B concerns recovery controls by financial entities after an ICT-related incident.
verdict.evidence_span_a: is aansprakelijk voor de schade die wordt veroorzaakt door verwerking die inbreuk maakt op deze verordening
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij herstel van een ICT-gerelateerd incident verrichten financiële entiteiten de benodigde controles, ook meerdere controles, waaronder afstemmingen, om ervoor te zorgen dat het hoogste niveau van gegevensintegriteit wordt gehandhaafd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the responsible entity to communicate information to an external recipient: Norm A requires a financial entity to promptly inform clients about a serious ICT-related incident and mitigation measures (and, where applicable, protective measures concerning a significant cyber threat); Norm B requires an AI deployer to notify the market-surveillance authority of the results of a fundamental-rights impact assessment and submit the completed template.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is client-facing incident/cyber-threat communication triggered by a serious ICT incident or significant cyber threat; Norm B is an authority-facing notification of a pre-use fundamental-rights impact assessment for certain high-risk AI systems, including a prescribed template.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different triggering events, different actor roles, different recipients, and materially different information: incident and mitigation/protection information to clients versus assessment results and a statutory template to a market-surveillance authority. The shared verb-level act of notifying is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen zien op het verstrekken van informatie over een ICT-/cyberincident, maar A vereist rapportage aan een CSIRT of bevoegde autoriteit, terwijl B kennisgeving aan getroffen cliënten vereist.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft een formele, gefaseerde incidentrapportage aan een overheids- of incidentresponsautoriteit, met specifieke inhoud en termijnen; norm B betreft onverwijlde cliëntcommunicatie over het incident en genomen beperkende maatregelen.
verdict.criterion_fired: Zelfde incidentfamilie en actorrol, maar verschillende ontvangers, doeleinden en inhoud: autoriteitsrapportage met technische/operationele incidentgegevens versus cliëntkennisgeving over het incident en beschermende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern compliance following a serious/significant ICT-related incident, but A requires urgent notification to service recipients, whereas B requires post-incident evaluation, root-cause analysis, identification of improvements, and—under its second paragraph—communication of implemented changes to competent authorities on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an outward incident notification to the entity’s service recipients; Norm B is an internal post-incident review and improvement process, with possible later disclosure of resulting changes to competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The event family is related, but the core actions, actor scope, and required content/purpose are materially different; A communicates the incident itself to service recipients, while B evaluates the disruption and implements or reports improvements.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten
verdict.evidence_span_b: verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, analyseren daarbij de oorzaken van de verstoring en identificeren de verbeteringen die moeten worden aangebracht

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose obligations connected broadly to digital/ICT risk, but A requires notifying an affected person of a personal-data breach, whereas B requires establishing, maintaining, and evaluating a comprehensive digital-operational-resilience testing programme.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an immediate, event-triggered notification duty to the affected data subject; Norm B is an ongoing governance and testing-programme duty for certain financial entities, not a breach notification duty.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering framework, and actor scope: A requires breach notification to a data subject, while B requires a resilience-testing programme. They are not the same compliance work repeated.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A vereist het implementeren en onderhouden van technische, operationele en organisatorische beveiligingsmaatregelen; norm B vereist het melden van ernstige incidenten aan markttoezichtautoriteiten, met aanvullende onderzoek-, samenwerkings- en corrigerende verplichtingen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een preventieve risicobeheersings- en beveiligingsmaatregelenplicht voor aanbieders van openbare elektronische communicatienetwerken of -diensten. Norm B is een incidentmeldingsplicht voor aanbieders van hoog-risico-AI-systemen, met specifieke termijnen en markttoezichtautoriteiten als ontvangers.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie en de actorcategorie verschillen: maatregelen nemen ter beheersing van beveiligingsrisico’s versus ernstige incidenten melden; de gedeelde incident-/beveiligingscontext is onvoldoende om van dezelfde compliance-werkzaamheden te spreken.
verdict.evidence_span_a: nemen bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur vastgestelde technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van hun netwerken of diensten te beheersen
verdict.evidence_span_b: melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A verplicht het melden van een significant incident aan een CSIRT en bevoegde autoriteit; norm B verplicht het uitvoeren van passende tests van ICT-instrumenten en -systemen.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een incidentmeldingsplicht met een termijn van onverwijld of uiterlijk 72 uur (of, voor bepaalde vertrouwensdienstaanbieders, 24 uur); norm B is een preventieve/periodieke testplicht zonder in deze bepaling genoemde deadline of meldingsontvanger.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie, het triggering event en de aard van de betrokken actor verschillen wezenlijk: melden van een reeds vastgesteld significant incident tegenover het uitvoeren van ICT-weerbaarheidstests.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: in de uitvoering van passende tests, zoals kwetsbaarheidsbeoordelingen en -scans

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an essential or important entity to stop using, and exclusively use products or services other than those supplied by a designated risky party. B requires a financial entity to report serious ICT-related incidents, including initial, interim, and final reports, to the relevant competent authority using prescribed models and information.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is a preventive procurement/use restriction concerning suppliers and products or services; B is an incident-reporting and notification duty concerning serious ICT-related incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different core actions on different actor categories and address different triggering circumstances: A concerns ministerially imposed supplier restrictions to manage national-security risks or prevent incidents, whereas B concerns financial-entity reporting after serious ICT-related incidents.
verdict.evidence_span_a: legt hij in overeenstemming met Onze Minister een essentiële entiteit of een belangrijke entiteit de verplichting op om in de daarbij aangewezen onderdelen van haar netwerk- en informatiesystemen uitsluitend gebruik te maken van producten of diensten van anderen dan de daarbij door Onze Minister die het aangaat genoemde partij
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address security/significant incidents affecting services, but A requires urgent notification of service recipients, whereas B requires implementation of prescribed technical, operational, and organisational security-risk measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-triggered information duty to customers/service recipients; Norm B is an ongoing or preventive risk-management duty involving security measures, with no reporting recipient or deadline specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action and actor scope: A imposes urgent customer notification on essential or important entities after significant service-impacting incidents; B imposes security measures on public electronic communications network/service providers to limit consequences for national security or public order.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: nemen bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur vastgestelde technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van hun netwerken of diensten te beheersen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern ICT/security-incident-related reporting or follow-up, but Norm A imposes a substitute progress report and later final report on an essential or important entity, whereas Norm B primarily describes supervisory feedback and preserves the financial entity’s responsibility; it does not impose the same report on the financial entity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty owed to the CSIRT and competent authority, with specified report content and deadlines. Norm B is a supervisory-feedback/responsibility provision concerning reports under Article 19 and does not itself require the financial entity to submit an equivalent report.
verdict.criterion_fired: The provisions address the same broad ICT-incident family and comparable regulated-entity roles, but they do not impose the same underlying verb-level action: A requires submission of progress/final reports, while B concerns the authority’s feedback and the entity’s continuing responsibility, without imposing an equivalent reporting obligation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in waarin wordt ingegaan op de aspecten, genoemd in het eerste lid
verdict.evidence_span_b: blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern handling ICT/security incidents, including an incident-related reporting element, but Norm A requires a specific external incident notification/reporting sequence while Norm B requires establishing and implementing an internal ICT-incident management process that includes reporting as one component.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes an event-triggered external reporting duty for significant incidents affecting a trust service, with a 24-hour deadline and specified warning/report content. Norm B imposes an ongoing organizational/process duty on financial entities to design, adopt, and implement an ICT-incident management process; it does not itself require a particular incident report to a named authority or set a reporting deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in their core action and actor role: A is an external, time-bound notification/reporting obligation imposed on a trust-service provider for a significant incident; B is a standing process-design and implementation obligation imposed on financial entities. The shared ICT-incident subject matter and B's inclusion of reporting within the process do not make the same compliance work repeat.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to submit a final incident report (or, while the incident continues, a progress report followed by a final report) to its CSIRT and competent authority. Norm B concerns the lead overseer imposing a daily penalty on a critical ICT third-party service provider until obligations are fulfilled, for up to six months.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty imposed on an essential or important entity; Norm B is an enforcement power involving daily coercive penalties imposed by a lead overseer on a critical ICT third-party service provider. They do not impose the same compliance work.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, event context, and actor role; Norm A concerns reporting an incident, whereas Norm B concerns imposing an enforcement penalty for non-compliance.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 6 bedoelde dwangsom wordt dagelijks opgelegd tot aan de verplichtingen is voldaan, gedurende een termijn van ten hoogste zes maanden volgend op de kennisgeving van het besluit een dwangsom op te leggen aan de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an essential or important entity to report every significant incident under Articles 26–29. B requires a financial entity, other than a micro-enterprise, to provide competent authorities on request with information about changes implemented after post-incident evaluations following serious ICT-related disruptions.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an incident-reporting duty covering every significant incident; B is a post-incident follow-up information duty, triggered only by an authority request and limited to implemented changes after an evaluation.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad ICT-incident family and broadly comparable regulated-entity role, but different core actions and substantially different content/purpose: incident notification versus requested disclosure of post-evaluation changes.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident
verdict.evidence_span_b: delen op verzoek de bevoegde autoriteiten de wijzigingen mee die na de in de eerste alinea bedoelde ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties zijn doorgevoerd

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to a harmful cyber/AI-related event, but A requires urgent information-sharing with potentially affected service recipients, whereas B requires reporting a serious incident to the national market-surveillance authority and taking risk-mitigation, suspension, or recall measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a service-recipient warning duty concerning measures recipients can take in response to a significant cyber threat; Norm B is a regulatory incident-reporting and operational risk-control duty concerning serious incidents found during real-world testing of high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, actor role, recipient, and substantive purpose: A communicates protective measures and possibly the threat to affected service recipients, while B reports a serious testing incident to a market-surveillance authority and requires mitigation, suspension, or termination/recall procedures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve producing and supplying information to a public authority in the context of digital/security governance, but A requires responsive or proactive provision of data and information needed by the Minister, whereas B requires documenting and evaluating the ICT-risk-management framework and, on request, supplying an evaluation report.

Norm B is primarily a recurring ICT-risk-management documentation and evaluation duty, with a report supplied to the competent authority only upon request.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller to notify the competent supervisory authority of a personal-data breach; B requires financial entities to perform checks and reconciliations during ICT-incident recovery or data reconstruction to maintain data integrity.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling ICT/AI-related incidents, but Norm A requires covered financial entities to ensure that ICT incidents can be handled quickly, whereas Norm B requires reporting a serious incident to a designated national competent authority.

verdict.criterion_fired: Same reporting action, incident family, and actor role, but the regimes use different incident thresholds and reporting frameworks, authorities, procedures, and required content; the text does not establish that the reports are identical or substantially duplicative.

verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external, time-bound early-warning/reporting duty concerning a significant incident; Norm B is an ongoing internal record-keeping duty concerning all personal-data breaches.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, actor role, recipient/purpose, and substantive content: A requires prompt notification to authorities/CSIRT, while B requires maintaining an internal overview.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A vereist het uitvoeren van ICT-tests binnen een testprogramma; norm B vereist het melden van ernstige incidenten aan markttoezichtautoriteiten.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require reporting/notifying a security- or incident-related event to a public authority, but they do not require the same substantive report: A concerns breaches or misuse involving the actor’s own electronic service, while B concerns serious incidents involving a high-risk AI system and requires reporting to market-surveillance authorities under specified AI Act conditions.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm B is an AI Act serious-incident reporting duty for providers (and in some cases deployers) of high-risk AI systems, with a 15-day maximum deadline and special two- or ten-day rules; Norm A is an immediate notification duty concerning compromise or misuse of the notifying entity’s own electronic service.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and materially different reportable event/content: A applies to a public authority or designated organisation reporting compromise or misuse of its own electronic service; B applies to providers or, in specified cases, deployers reporting serious incidents involving a high-risk AI system to market-surveillance authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a controller to promptly communicate a personal-data breach to the data subject; B requires a financial entity to maintain and regularly test mechanisms for promptly detecting anomalous activities, ICT incidents and network-performance issues, and identifying physical single points of failure.

verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A is breach notification by a data controller to a data subject, whereas B is implementation and testing of detection mechanisms by a financial entity. The shared incident-related context is insufficient to create duplicate compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern dealing with/reporting ICT-related incidents: Norm A requires financial entities to register all ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats and establish processes for monitoring, treatment, follow-up, and root-cause remediation; Norm B requires providers or, where applicable, deployers of high-risk AI systems to report serious incidents to market-surveillance authorities, immediately and no later than two days after awareness in the specified widespread-breach or serious-incident case.

Norm B is an external, authority-facing notification duty for high-risk AI providers/deployers, triggered by serious incidents and subject to a specific deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern a broadly similar incident family, but they impose materially different actions on different regulated actor roles: internal registration and management by financial entities versus external reporting by high-risk AI providers/deployers. The shared incident theme and authority-facing character of Norm B do not establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het verkrijgen of verstrekken van informatie over ICT-gerelateerde risico’s of incidenten, maar norm A verplicht het leidinggevend orgaan interne meldingskanalen op te zetten om informatie binnen de onderneming in te winnen, terwijl norm B een externe meldplicht bij een aangewezen CSIRT voorschrijft.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to an incident-like event, but A requires maintaining a register of all personal-data breaches, whereas B requires reporting each serious incident found during real-world testing to the national market-surveillance authority and taking immediate risk-mitigation/testing-termination measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address cybersecurity/security risks, but A requires urgent communication to potentially affected service recipients, whereas B requires implementation of prescribed technical, operational, and organisational security measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve communicating information about cyber/data-related incidents, but A requires prompt notification of a personal-data breach to the controller, whereas B requires the national central contact point to submit a periodic, anonymised and aggregated summary to ENISA concerning reported significant incidents, incidents, cyber threats and near-incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an immediate processor-to-controller personal-data-breach notification; Norm B is a quarterly central-contact-point-to-ENISA aggregation and reporting duty covering a broader set of incidents and threats.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core reporting action: A is an immediate notification by a processor to a controller, while B is a quarterly aggregated report by a central contact point to ENISA. The shared incident-related subject matter and broadly institutional recipient relationship do not make the underlying compliance work the same.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report instead of the final report while an incident continues, followed by a final report within one month after resolution. B requires a financial entity to classify cyber threats as significant based on specified risk and impact factors.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is a reporting/submission duty concerning an ongoing incident and its description, causes, mitigation measures, and effects; B is an internal classification/assessment duty concerning the significance of cyber threats, with no reporting recipient or deadline stated.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A requires incident reporting by an essential or important entity to its CSIRT and competent authority, whereas B requires a financial entity to classify cyber threats as significant. The shared cyber/security context is insufficient to establish duplicated or merely related reporting burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve supplying information to a public authority, but Norm A requires a structured final/progress incident report, while Norm B requires supplying data and information needed by the Minister to prevent or end infringements concerning secure and reliable electronic access.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a time-bound incident-reporting duty imposed on essential or important entities and directed to both the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority; Norm B is an on-request or spontaneous information-supply duty imposed on a broader set of regulated actors and directed to the Minister for supervisory/intervention purposes.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in the triggering event/purpose, actor class, and substantive content: Norm A concerns reporting a cybersecurity incident and its consequences and mitigation, whereas Norm B concerns information needed to prevent or terminate infringements involving secure and reliable electronic access.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the controller to report a personal-data breach to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours where applicable; B requires the financial entity’s ICT test programme to carry out specified ICT-resilience tests, with risk-based planning and resource/time balancing for micro-enterprises.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an incident-notification duty to a supervisory authority; B is a preventive ICT-testing and planning duty, with no reporting recipient or incident-triggered notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in core action, triggering event, and compliance purpose: breach notification versus implementation of an ICT testing programme.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an electronic communications provider to promptly notify the Dutch Data Protection Authority of a qualifying personal-data security breach. Norm B requires non-micro financial entities to establish, maintain, and evaluate a comprehensive digital-operational-resilience testing programme, using a risk-based approach, to assess incident-handling readiness and identify weaknesses and corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an immediate breach-notification duty to a supervisory authority; Norm B is an ongoing internal governance and testing-programme duty for a different regulated sector, with no reporting recipient or incident-triggered notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, operative action, and event structure: notification of a qualifying personal-data security breach versus establishment and operation of a resilience-testing programme. The shared ICT/security theme is insufficient to create duplicate or related compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A legt schadeaansprakelijkheid op voor onrechtmatige verwerking, terwijl norm B een ICT-risicobeheerkader en operationele beveiligingsmaatregelen vereist, waaronder het verwerken van test- en incidentanalyseconclusies in het risicobeoordelingsproces.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een aansprakelijkheidsregel die een rechtsgevolg koppelt aan schade door GDPR-inbreuk; norm B is een preventieve en organisatorisch-technische ICT-risicobeheerplicht voor bepaalde financiële entiteiten.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben geen dezelfde kernactie of hetzelfde type trigger: A betreft aansprakelijkheid voor schade door verwerking in strijd met de AVG; B betreft doorlopend ICT-risicobeheer, toezicht, incidentafhandeling en het opnemen van conclusies in een risicobeoordelingsproces.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires providers of public electronic communications networks/services to implement technical, operational, and organisational security-risk measures to limit the effects of security incidents. B requires reporting each serious incident found during real-world testing to the national market-surveillance authority, plus immediate mitigation, suspension/termination, and recall procedures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is a preventive, ongoing security-risk management obligation for electronic communications providers; B is an incident-triggered reporting and response obligation for providers or potential providers testing high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different core actions on different actor roles in different operational contexts: A requires preventive security measures for electronic communications networks/services, whereas B requires reporting and responding to serious incidents during real-world testing of high-risk AI systems.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires notifying the Dutch Data Protection Authority and affected data subjects about a personal-data breach, including its nature, information sources, recommended mitigation, and—toward the authority—its consequences and response measures. B requires financial entities to maintain and regularly test mechanisms for promptly detecting anomalous activities, ICT incidents, network-performance issues, and physical single points of failure.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an external notification and information-content duty following a personal-data breach; B is an internal ICT-risk detection capability and testing duty, not an incident-reporting obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different verb-level duties and address different compliance objects: breach notification and disclosure versus establishing and testing detection mechanisms. They also concern different triggering/event structures and actor populations; any superficial ICT-incident overlap does not make the underlying work the same.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen betreffen ICT/cyberrisico’s, maar norm A verplicht een concrete melding van een significant incident aan een CSIRT of bevoegde autoriteit; norm B verplicht preventief en doorlopend ICT-risicobeheer, waaronder detectie en snelle afhandeling van incidenten.

verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie en actorrol verschillen: A betreft rapporteren door een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten aan een CSIRT/bevoegde autoriteit; B betreft ICT-risicobeheer door bepaalde financiële entiteiten. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve communicating information to a competent authority, but A requires an incident notification with incident-related information, whereas B requires—only on request—communicating changes implemented after a post-incident evaluation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an immediate statutory notification of a significant incident to the CSIRT and competent authority, including specified incident details. Norm B is a request-based disclosure to competent authorities of remedial changes made after an ICT post-incident evaluation; it is not an incident notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in their core action and actor scope: A requires essential or important entities to report a significant incident promptly, with incident assessment and impact information; B requires non-micro financial entities, upon request, to communicate implemented post-evaluation changes. The shared incident-related context and authority recipient do not make the compliance work the same.
