verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require reporting an ICT/security incident to a CSIRT, but Norm A requires a trust-service provider to report a significant incident affecting its trust services to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours, whereas Norm B requires specified financial-sector entities to make the DORA Article 19 mandatory or voluntary report additionally to the designated sectoral CSIRT.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties apply to different actor categories and are tied to different underlying reporting regimes: trust-service providers and NIS2 significant incidents under Norm A, versus specified financial-market entities and DORA Article 19 reports under Norm B. Norm B's text does not establish that its report has the same content or deadline as Norm A's 24-hour early-warning/incident-reporting sequence.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role, with insufficient textual basis to treat the underlying reports as the same compliance work; the shared incident-reporting theme and CSIRT recipient do not overcome that distinction.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to an incident by supplying incident-related information to a public authority, but Norm A requires internal documentation of personal-data breaches, whereas Norm B requires time-bound incident reporting and follow-up reports to a CSIRT or competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a documentation and auditability duty concerning personal-data breaches; Norm B is an operational, staged reporting duty concerning significant incidents affecting service provision, with specified deadlines and incident-assessment, impact, threat, and mitigation information.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad security/incident family and overlapping incident facts, consequences, and corrective or mitigating measures, but the actor scope, legal purpose, procedural form, recipient, and required reporting package differ; therefore this is related compliance work rather than the same work repeated.

verdict.evidence_span_b: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires designated public-sector bodies and other specified eID-related actors to provide the Minister, on request and proactively, data and information needed to prevent or end infringements of secure and reliable access to electronic services. B requires the management body of a financial entity to establish governance arrangements and enterprise-level reporting channels enabling it to obtain information about ICT third-party arrangements, material changes, impacts on critical or important functions, serious ICT incidents, consequences, and response, recovery, and corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an information-provision duty to a Minister concerning threats or infringements affecting secure and reliable access to electronic services; B is an internal ICT-risk governance and information-channel duty imposed on a financial entity's management body, with no external recipient or incident-reporting deadline specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action on the same actor role: A requires supplying information externally to a Minister, whereas B requires establishing internal governance/reporting channels and related oversight arrangements. The shared ICT/security context is insufficient for duplicate burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, op grond van artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houders van een erkenning en op grond van artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgevers en diensten verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling and communicating information about incidents, including measures to address or mitigate their consequences. Norm A requires notification of a personal-data breach with specified content to the Dutch data-protection authority and affected person; Norm B requires providers of systemic-risk general-purpose AI models to keep and document relevant information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures, and report it without delay to the AI Office and, where applicable, national competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns notification of a personal-data breach and includes affected individuals as recipients, with prescribed breach details and mitigation recommendations. Norm B concerns recordkeeping, documentation, and prompt reporting of serious incidents and possible corrective measures by a specific class of AI-model provider, directed to AI authorities. The duties therefore differ in incident scope, content, purpose, and partly in actor and recipients.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core compliance action on the same actor role: A is a personal-data-breach notification duty, while B is a combined retention/documentation and urgent reporting duty for systemic-risk GPAI providers concerning serious incidents. Although both involve incident information and corrective or mitigating measures, the actor scope, incident category, required content, and regulatory purpose differ materially.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving aan de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens en de persoon wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft, omvat in ieder geval de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms involve documenting/evaluating or documenting and reporting information connected with serious ICT/AI-related risks or incidents, but they do not require the same underlying compliance work. Norm A requires documenting and evaluating the ICT-risk-management framework, with a report to the competent authority only upon request. Norm B requires providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk to keep, document, and promptly report relevant information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures to the AI Office and, where applicable, national competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns periodic or incident-triggered evaluation of an entity-wide ICT risk-management framework and an on-request evaluation report; Norm B concerns maintaining and promptly reporting information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures for systemic-risk general-purpose AI models.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action/content: A concerns ICT-risk-management-framework evaluation and an on-request report, while B concerns maintaining, documenting, and promptly reporting serious-incident and corrective-measure information. Similar incident-related triggering language and authority recipients do not make the obligations duplicative.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt ten minste eenmaal per jaar, of periodiek in het geval van micro-ondernemingen, gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd, alsook wanneer zich ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten voordoen
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an essential or important entity to use only products or services other than those identified by the Minister; B requires a processor to inform the controller of a personal-data breach without undue delay.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is a minister-imposed supply/use restriction aimed at managing national-security risks or preventing national-security incidents, whereas B is a processor-to-controller notification duty following a personal-data breach.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, operative action, and triggering event: A imposes a product/service-use restriction on an essential or important entity in response to national-security concerns; B requires a processor to notify the controller after learning of a personal-data breach.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern communicating information about an incident, but A is an early warning containing specified incident characteristics and a responsible officer’s contact details, while B is a substantive report of a serious incident to a designated national competent authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to give an early warning to its CSIRT and competent authority, without delay or within 24 hours, including whether the significant incident was likely caused by an unlawful or malicious act, whether it may have cross-border effects, and the responsible reporting officer’s contact details. Norm B requires reporting qualifying serious incidents involving certain high-risk AI systems to the designated national competent authority where the incident occurred; it does not specify the same warning content or deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern different regulated actors and distinct reporting regimes: A applies to essential or important entities reporting significant incidents through an early-warning process to a CSIRT and competent authority, whereas B applies to providers or other responsible actors for specified high-risk AI systems and reports serious incidents to a designated national competent authority. The shared incident-reporting theme and possible authority overlap do not establish the same compliance duty.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern communicating information and recommended protective measures in response to a harmful cyber/data incident. However, Norm A requires the service provider to promptly inform potentially affected service recipients about measures they can take in response to a significant cyber threat, while Norm B specifies the contents of a notification to the Dutch Data Protection Authority and the affected data subject concerning a personal-data breach, including its nature, information sources, consequences, and mitigation measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent warning to potentially affected service recipients about a significant cyber threat related to the services. Norm B is a personal-data-breach notification with prescribed content, addressed to the supervisory authority and affected individual(s), including breach consequences and the provider's response measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad incident-response communication pattern, but the actor role is not established as the same and the recipients, notification purpose, and required content differ materially; therefore this is related rather than the same reporting work repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De kennisgeving aan de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens en de persoon wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft, omvat in ieder geval de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de instanties waar meer informatie over de inbreuk kan worden verkregen en de aanbevolen maatregelen om de negatieve gevolgen van de inbreuk te beperken.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require communication concerning a security/personal-data incident, but A requires an incident progress report or final report containing operational and technical details to the CSIRT and competent authority, while B requires prompt communication of a high-risk personal-data breach to the affected data subject, subject to exceptions or equivalent public communication.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty by an essential or important entity to institutional authorities, including a progress report when the incident continues and a final report after resolution. Norm B is a data-subject notification duty by a controller, triggered by a likely high risk to individuals' rights and freedoms and directed to the affected data subject.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern a broadly related incident family but differ in actor role, core action, recipient, trigger threshold, purpose, and required content; this is not the same compliance work repeated for another recipient.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Communicate/report an incident: Norm A requires the controller to communicate a personal-data breach to the data subject; Norm B requires the provider or, where applicable, deployer to report a serious incident to market-surveillance authorities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to ICT/security-related risks or incidents, but Norm A requires reporting a personal-data breach to a supervisory authority, whereas Norm B requires incorporating operational lessons from tests and incident analysis into the ICT-risk-assessment process.

Norm B is an internal ICT-risk-management and learning-process duty, with no recipient or deadline specified in the norm.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, actor roles, recipients, and compliance purposes differ materially: external notification of a personal-data breach versus internal incorporation of lessons from tests and incident analysis into risk assessment.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires public electronic communications providers to implement proportionate technical, operational, and organisational security measures; Norm B requires financial entities to classify cyber threats as significant.

verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor roles and different core actions; the shared cyber/security subject matter is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the regulated entity to report a serious/significant ICT or cyber incident to a competent authority, with incident information enabling assessment of its scope, impact, and possible cross-border effects. However, Article 19 also entails a DORA-specific first notification, intermediate updates, and final report using prescribed models and within Article 20 deadlines, while Article 27 includes reporting to both the CSIRT and competent authority and additional information such as indicators of compromise and an initial assessment.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The regimes differ in scope and reporting architecture: NIS2 Article 27 applies to essential or important entities and requires a prompt/72-hour report to both CSIRT and competent authority; DORA Article 19 applies to financial entities and requires a staged, model-based reporting process to the relevant financial competent authority, with possible onward transmission or additional national reporting.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same actor role and same ICT/cyber-incident event family, but the reporting content, recipient structure, and staged procedure differ sufficiently that the texts do not establish the same report being submitted twice. The overlap is a related reporting burden rather than DUPLICATE_BURDEN.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require prompt communication concerning an incident, but A requires an essential or important entity to report every significant incident under Articles 26–29, while B requires a processor to inform the controller upon becoming aware of a personal-data breach.

Norm B is a processor-to-controller notification duty specifically for a personal-data breach, triggered by the processor's awareness and owed without undue delay.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and materially different duty: A concerns an essential/important entity reporting significant incidents under the NIS framework; B concerns a processor informing its controller of a personal-data breach. The shared incident-related trigger and communication form do not make the compliance work the same.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the relevant entity to implement technical, operational, and/or organisational cybersecurity risk-management measures protecting networks or information systems against security incidents and limiting their consequences.

verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role: Norm A applies to the entity subject to the NIS2-style general cybersecurity duty, whereas Norm B applies specifically to providers of public electronic communications networks or services. The duties concern related security-risk mitigation but are not the same obligation imposed on the same actor role.

verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, triggering event, actor role and substantive content; the superficial similarity is limited to dealing with risk-related information.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to send an early warning about a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority, including specified incident-cause, cross-border-impact, and contact information. Norm B gives an injured person a right to receive compensation from a controller or processor for damage caused by a GDPR infringement; it imposes no comparable reporting or notification duty on the entity.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting/early-warning duty imposed on an essential or important entity; Norm B is a private compensation entitlement for a person suffering damage from a GDPR infringement.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in operative action, triggering event, and duty-holder: early-warning reporting of a significant incident by an essential/important entity versus receiving compensation by a person harmed by a GDPR infringement.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Eenieder die materiële of immateriële schade heeft geleden ten gevolge van een inbreuk op deze verordening, heeft het recht om van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker schadevergoeding te ontvangen voor de geleden schade.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen zien op ICT-gerelateerde compliance na of in verband met een ICT-incident, maar norm A vereist incidentmelding aan een CSIRT/bevoegde autoriteit; norm B vereist documentatie en evaluatie van het ICT-risicobeheerkader en indiening van een evaluatieverslag op verzoek.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een tijdgebonden externe incidentrapportageplicht voor betrokken entiteiten (met voor vertrouwensdiensten een termijn van 24 uur). Norm B is een periodieke of incident-geactiveerde interne governance-/risicobeheer-evaluatieplicht voor financiële entiteiten, met een verslag op verzoek van de bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.criterion_fired: The core action and actor role differ: A requires reporting a significant incident and its details to an incident-response authority, whereas B requires documenting and evaluating an ICT-risk-management framework; the shared ICT-incident context is insufficient to create duplicate compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern making a notification/report following an incident or breach, but A requires substantive breach information to be communicated to the Dutch data-protection authority and affected person, whereas B requires providers of high-risk AI systems (and, where applicable, deployers) to report serious incidents to market-surveillance authorities within a shortened deadline.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a personal-data-breach notification with specified content and dual recipients; Norm B is a serious AI-incident report to market-surveillance authorities, with a two-day deadline triggered by awareness and a different actor scope and reporting purpose.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and materially different reporting content and regulatory purpose; the shared incident-reporting form and broad incident trigger do not make the underlying compliance duty the same.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving aan de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens en de persoon wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft, omvat in ieder geval de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the responsible actor to communicate or make information available to a public authority, but Norm A requires documentation of personal-data breaches for supervisory compliance, whereas Norm B requires notification of a fundamental-rights impact-assessment result together with a completed template to the market-surveillance authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns documenting all personal-data breaches, including facts, consequences, and corrective measures; Norm B concerns notifying the results of a pre-deployment fundamental-rights impact assessment for certain high-risk AI systems and submitting a prescribed template.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern different triggering events, different responsible actor roles, and materially different information and regulatory purposes; a shared authority-facing communication pattern is insufficient to establish duplicate compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve communicating incident-related information to a competent authority, but A requires an incident notification while B requires, only on request, an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an immediate notification duty for a significant incident affecting a trust service, addressed to both the CSIRT and competent authority, with specified incident details. Norm B is a request-based provision of an annual aggregate cost-and-loss estimate by certain financial entities to competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor scope and core action: A requires prompt incident reporting by trust-service essential or important entities, whereas B requires other financial entities to provide an aggregated annual cost/loss estimate on request. The shared incident-related context and competent-authority recipient do not make the compliance work the same.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an administrative body or designated organisation to promptly notify the Minister and provide all necessary information about a security/integrity breach or misuse of access to its own electronic service. B requires the management body of a financial entity to establish governance arrangements and enterprise-level reporting channels for obtaining information about ICT-service-provider arrangements, planned material changes, their effects, incidents, and response/recovery/corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an incident-triggered notification duty to a Minister; B is an ongoing ICT-governance and internal information-channel duty imposed on the management body of a financial entity, not an incident notification to an external authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same core action, are not triggered by the same event family, and do not bind the same actor role. A concerns urgent external reporting of a security or access incident; B concerns establishing internal governance/reporting channels and obtaining ICT-risk information.

verdict.evidence_span_b: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A: meld een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens aan de bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit. B: deel op verzoek met bevoegde autoriteiten de wijzigingen die na ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties zijn doorgevoerd.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A vereist een tijdige incidentmelding met een specifieke 72-uursdeadline en ziet op een persoonsgegevensinbreuk. Norm B vereist, alleen op verzoek, mededeling van doorgevoerde wijzigingen na een post-incident-evaluatie; de evaluatie betreft oorzaken, verbeteringen, gevolgde procedures en doeltreffendheid van maatregelen.
verdict.criterion_fired: Zelfde algemene incidentfamilie en dezelfde actorcategorie, maar niet dezelfde kernhandeling of inhoud: een verplichte melding van een persoonsgegevensinbreuk binnen 72 uur tegenover het op verzoek delen van wijzigingen na een ICT-post-incidentevaluatie.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen delen op verzoek de bevoegde autoriteiten de wijzigingen mee die na de in de eerste alinea bedoelde ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties zijn doorgevoerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires financial entities to deploy sufficient resources and capabilities to monitor user activity and ICT anomalies/incidents, especially cyberattacks. Norm B requires reporting each serious incident identified during real-world testing to the national market-surveillance authority, plus immediate mitigation, suspension/termination, and recall procedures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a continuous ICT-monitoring capability duty for financial entities; Norm B is an incident-reporting and incident-response duty for providers or prospective providers of high-risk AI systems during real-world testing.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in the core action, triggering-event context, and obligated actor: continuous monitoring of ICT activity/incidents by financial entities versus reporting and responding to serious incidents during real-world high-risk AI testing by AI providers or prospective providers.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten zetten voldoende middelen en capaciteiten in om toezicht te houden op activiteiten van gebruikers en het optreden van ICT-anomalieën en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, met name cyberaanvallen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A imposes liability for damage caused by processing that infringes the GDPR; Norm B requires certain financial entities, on request, to communicate to competent authorities the changes implemented after ICT-related post-incident evaluations.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a substantive liability rule concerning compensation for unlawful processing, whereas Norm B is a post-incident information-sharing duty concerning implemented improvements after a serious ICT incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, event family, and actor role; the norms do not require the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern compliance activity connected with ICT/security incidents, but A requires promptly informing service recipients about significant incidents, whereas B requires documenting and evaluating the ICT-risk-management framework and providing an evaluation report to the competent authority on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident communication duty directed to service recipients; Norm B is a recurring and incident-triggered ICT-risk-management evaluation/documentation duty, with a report to the competent authority only upon request.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same general ICT-incident/event family and same regulated-entity role, but different verb-level actions, recipients, purposes, and substantive content; therefore related compliance burden rather than duplicated reporting.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern action taken in response to an ICT/personal-data incident, but A requires urgent notification of affected individuals, whereas B requires financial entities to perform data-integrity checks during recovery or reconstruction.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an individual data-subject notification duty triggered by a qualifying personal-data breach; Norm B is an internal recovery/control duty concerning data integrity after an ICT-related incident.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action and actor role differ: A requires a provider to notify the affected person, while B requires financial entities to perform recovery-stage data-integrity controls. The shared incident context is insufficient to make the compliance work duplicative.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern reporting a qualifying incident to a public authority, but they do not establish the same underlying reporting duty: Norm A imposes a duty on an essential or important entity to report every significant incident under Articles 26–29, while Norm B limits reporting for specified high-risk AI systems to defined serious incidents and directs the report to the designated national competent authority in the Member State where the incident occurred.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A applies to essential or important entities and covers every significant incident under Articles 26–29; Norm B applies to high-risk AI systems that are, or are safety components of, devices covered by Regulations (EU) 2017/745 and 2017/746, limits the reportable incidents to the incidents defined in Article 3(49)(c), and specifies a designated national competent authority in the place of occurrence.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and materially different scope/content of the reporting duty; the shared incident-reporting form and broad incident family are insufficient to establish duplicate compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voor AI-systemen met een hoog risico die veiligheidscomponenten van apparaten zijn of zelf apparaten zijn die onder de Verordeningen (EU) 2017/745 en (EU) 2017/746 vallen, wordt de melding van ernstige incidenten beperkt tot de in artikel 3, punt 49), c), van de onderhavige verordening bedoelde incidenten, en wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern a response connected to a cyber/ICT-related situation, but they do not impose the same compliance action: Norm A requires an entity to promptly inform potentially affected service recipients about protective measures (and, if necessary, the threat); Norm B concerns the lead overseer imposing a daily coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider until obligations are fulfilled.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an information duty owed by an essential or important entity to its service recipients. Norm B is an enforcement power exercised by the lead overseer against a critical ICT third-party provider; it is not a reporting or notification duty of the provider.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in both actor role and operative action: informing service recipients about measures against a significant cyber threat versus imposing a daily coercive fine as an enforcement measure.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 6 bedoelde dwangsom wordt dagelijks opgelegd tot aan de verplichtingen is voldaan, gedurende een termijn van ten hoogste zes maanden

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires the central contact point to submit a quarterly anonymised, aggregated summary report to ENISA concerning previously reported incidents, cyber threats and near-incidents. B requires financial entities to classify cyber threats as significant; it does not impose a reporting duty.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a periodic reporting duty imposed on a central contact point and directed to ENISA. Norm B is a substantive classification duty imposed on financial entities, with no recipient or deadline specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different core action; the shared cyber-threat/incident subject matter is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern security-related compliance by an organizational/service-provider actor, but A requires immediate notification and information provision to the Minister, whereas B requires implementation of technical, operational, and organizational security measures to manage risks and reduce incident impacts.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident/misuse notification duty with an urgent deadline and a governmental recipient; Norm B is a preventive and resilience-oriented security-measures duty with no reporting recipient or deadline specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A imposes an immediate incident notification and information-supply duty on a public authority or designated organization, while B imposes a security-measures duty on providers of public electronic communications services. The shared security-incident context is insufficient to make the compliance work duplicative.

Norm B concerns personal-data breaches and processor-to-controller notification, without the authority-reporting and specified-content duty shown here.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern cybersecurity/data-incident-related compliance, but Norm A requires implementing broad preventive and organizational security measures, whereas Norm B requires including specified information in a personal-data-breach notification.

verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: Norm A requires an entity to implement and maintain protective measures, while Norm B requires a provider to include specified breach information in notifications. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require reporting an incident to a public authority, but A requires a trust-service provider to report a significant incident affecting its trust services, while B requires reporting a serious incident detected during real-world testing of a high-risk AI system and also imposes separate mitigation, suspension/termination, and recall-procedure duties.

The different authority is not decisive, but the norms do not establish the same or near-same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.

B requires providers of high-risk AI systems to report serious incidents to the relevant market-surveillance authorities, with immediate/short statutory deadlines and follow-up investigation and corrective measures.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling information connected with electronic/data-service events, but A requires immediate notification and accompanying information, whereas B requires maintaining systems to check transaction reports and request retransmission where needed.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde concrete compliance-actie: norm A vereist het uitvoeren van kwetsbaarheidsbeoordelingen vóór inzet of herinzet; norm B vereist het melden van een wijdverbreide inbreuk of ernstig incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern measures addressing ICT/network-security risks, but A requires an authority-imposed restriction on which supplier products or services an entity may use, whereas B requires financial entities to maintain crisis-communication plans enabling disclosure of serious ICT incidents or vulnerabilities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a supply-chain/product-and-service-use restriction imposed by a minister; Norm B is a crisis-communication planning and disclosure duty directed toward clients, counterparties, and potentially the public.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and duty-bearing actor roles differ: A concerns an essential or important entity being required to use products or services from permitted suppliers, while B concerns financial entities maintaining plans for communicating ICT incidents or vulnerabilities to external recipients.
verdict.evidence_span_a: legt hij in overeenstemming met Onze Minister een essentiële entiteit of een belangrijke entiteit de verplichting op om in de daarbij aangewezen onderdelen van haar netwerk- en informatiesystemen uitsluitend gebruik te maken van producten of diensten van anderen dan de daarbij door Onze Minister die het aangaat genoemde partij
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken financiële entiteiten over crisiscommunicatieplannen die het mogelijk maken ten minste ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten of kwetsbaarheden op verantwoordelijke wijze bekend te maken aan cliënten en tegenpartijen en, in voorkomend geval, aan het publiek

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require communication triggered by a serious incident: A requires a financial entity to inform potentially affected clients about the serious ICT-related incident and mitigation measures; B requires reporting a serious AI incident to market-surveillance authorities, with specified urgency and deadlines.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ fundamentally in recipient, actor context, and communicative purpose/content: client warning and mitigation advice under A versus regulatory incident reporting by high-risk AI providers or deployers under B.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and recipient/purpose; A is client notification concerning ICT incidents and mitigation, while B is regulatory reporting of serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling security/ICT incidents, but A requires notifying the Dutch Data Protection Authority of a qualifying personal-data security breach, whereas B requires financial entities to register all ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats and establish incident-management processes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external, urgent notification duty to a supervisory authority concerning a security breach affecting personal-data protection. Norm B is an internal registration and incident-management duty covering all ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats; it specifies no recipient or deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms share a broad incident-related subject matter, but they impose different core actions and different actor roles: A requires immediate external notification by a provider of a public electronic communications service, while B requires financial entities to register incidents and establish internal procedures and processes.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires public electronic communications providers to implement technical, operational, and organisational security measures. Norm B concerns the daily imposition of a coercive fine on a critical third-party ICT service provider following notification of a decision; it does not impose the same compliance action on the regulated actor.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a substantive preventive security-measures duty, whereas Norm B describes an enforcement sanction imposed by the lead overseer.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action: one requires implementation of security measures, while the other concerns an authority imposing a coercive fine.
verdict.evidence_span_a: nemen bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur vastgestelde technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address serious ICT/AI-related incidents, but Norm A requires financial entities to maintain crisis-communication plans enabling responsible disclosure to clients, counterparties, and possibly the public. Norm B requires reporting each serious incident found during real-world testing to the national market-surveillance authority, plus immediate risk mitigation, suspension, or termination procedures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing crisis-communication capability aimed at clients, counterparties, and potentially the public; Norm B is an incident-reporting and operational risk-response duty for providers or prospective providers conducting real-world AI testing, aimed at a market-surveillance authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The actor role and core action differ: Norm A concerns financial entities maintaining a communication plan for responsible disclosure to private stakeholders/public, while Norm B concerns AI-system providers or prospective providers reporting serious testing incidents to a national market-surveillance authority and taking immediate mitigation or testing-termination measures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: beschikken financiële entiteiten over crisiscommunicatieplannen die het mogelijk maken ten minste ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten of kwetsbaarheden op verantwoordelijke wijze bekend te maken aan cliënten en tegenpartijen en, in voorkomend geval, aan het publiek
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Geen gedeelde compliance-actie: norm A verplicht onverwijlde kennisgeving aan de betrokkene van een persoonsgegevensinbreuk; norm B verplicht uitvoering van passende tests binnen een programma voor digitale operationele weerbaarheid.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een incidentkennisgeving aan een persoon wiens persoonsgegevens zijn getroffen, terwijl norm B een preventieve/periodieke ICT-testverplichting voor financiële entiteiten betreft.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie, het type gebeurtenis, de normadressaat en het doel verschillen wezenlijk; een persoonsgegevensinbreuk activeert norm A, terwijl norm B het testen van ICT-instrumenten en -systemen voorschrijft.

verdict.evidence_span_b: voorziet, overeenkomstig de criteria in artikel 4, lid 2, in de uitvoering van passende tests

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating information about serious/significant ICT-related events, but Norm A requires the entity to report each significant incident under the statutory incident-reporting procedure, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to maintain crisis-communication plans enabling responsible disclosure to clients, counterparties, and potentially the public.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty under Articles 26–29, while Norm B is a preparedness and crisis-communication-plan requirement directed at communications with private stakeholders or the public, and also covers vulnerabilities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action on the same actor role: Norm A requires essential or important entities to report every significant incident through the statutory procedure, while Norm B requires financial entities to possess plans for responsible disclosure to clients, counterparties, or the public, including vulnerabilities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken financiële entiteiten over crisiscommunicatieplannen die het mogelijk maken ten minste ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten of kwetsbaarheden op verantwoordelijke wijze bekend te maken aan cliënten en tegenpartijen en, in voorkomend geval, aan het publiek.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Report a qualifying personal-data/security breach to a supervisory authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A applies to a public electronic communications service provider and requires immediate notification to the Dutch Data Protection Authority for a security breach adversely affecting personal-data protection; Norm B applies to a controller, covers personal-data breaches posing a risk to individuals, and requires notification to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours where possible, including reasons for delay if late.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same reporting action and breach-related event family, but the actor scope, qualifying threshold, reporting content, and deadline differ; therefore the texts indicate related rather than identical compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address ICT/cybersecurity risk, but Norm A requires urgent notification and information-sharing about a security or access-abuse incident, whereas Norm B requires ongoing identification and assessment of ICT risks, threats, vulnerabilities, and risk scenarios.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-notification duty to the Minister; Norm B is a continuous and periodic internal ICT-risk identification and assessment duty with no reporting recipient.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, triggering event, operative action, recipient, and compliance content: urgent incident notification versus continuous/annual risk assessment.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst
verdict.evidence_span_b: identificeren permanent alle bronnen van ICT-risico

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose obligations connected with serious/significant ICT incidents, but A requires rapid external incident reporting to a CSIRT or competent authority, whereas B requires an internal post-incident evaluation, root-cause analysis, identification of improvements, and—on request—communication of implemented changes to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an externally directed, time-bound incident-reporting duty; Norm B is an internal lessons-learned and remediation-review duty, with a separate request-based disclosure of resulting changes.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties concern the same broad ICT-incident context but require different core actions and serve different purposes: immediate regulatory notification versus internal evaluation and improvement.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, analyseren daarbij de oorzaken van de verstoring en identificeren de verbeteringen die moeten worden aangebracht

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern responding to or reporting an incident, but Norm A requires the provider to investigate a serious incident and take related measures, whereas Norm B requires specified financial-sector entities to submit an incident notification to a designated CSIRT.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent investigation and corrective-action duty following a serious AI incident; Norm B is an additional notification duty to a sectoral CSIRT concerning ICT incidents, including voluntary notifications.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action and actor role differ: Norm A requires investigation by a high-risk AI-system provider, while Norm B requires incident reporting by specified financial-sector entities. The shared incident context and authority-facing character do not make the compliance work the same.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem
verdict.evidence_span_b: doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the provider/entity to maintain or document information connected with operational or security-related events, but A requires a breach register while B requires documentation and evaluation of the ICT-risk-management framework, with a report to the competent authority only on request.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing register of all personal-data breaches, including specified facts and data; Norm B concerns periodic or event-triggered documentation and evaluation of the broader ICT-risk-management framework and possible reporting to a competent authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad ICT/security-incident context and comparable regulated-entity role, but the required work product and purpose differ substantially: a personal-data-breach register versus ICT-risk-management-framework evaluation/documentation and an on-request supervisory report.
verdict.evidence_span_a: houdt een overzicht bij van alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens. Dit overzicht bevat in elk geval de feiten en de in het derde lid bedoelde gegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt ten minste eenmaal per jaar, of periodiek in het geval van micro-ondernemingen, gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd, alsook wanneer zich ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten voordoen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to ICT/security-related incidents, but Norm A requires an incident report to the CSIRT and competent authority, while Norm B requires deploying resources and capabilities to monitor user activity and detect ICT anomalies and incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external incident-reporting duty triggered by a significant incident affecting a trust service, with a 24-hour deadline and specified reporting content. Norm B is an ongoing internal monitoring and detection measure for financial entities, with no recipient or deadline specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both core action and actor role: Norm A imposes rapid reporting by an essential or important trust-service entity to authorities, whereas Norm B imposes monitoring/detection capabilities on financial entities. The shared incident/security context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: zetten voldoende middelen en capaciteiten in om toezicht te houden op activiteiten van gebruikers en het optreden van ICT-anomalieën en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve communicating information in the broad sense, but Norm A requires an entity to promptly inform potentially affected service recipients about measures to take in response to a significant cyber threat, whereas Norm B requires specified public bodies and recognized entities to provide the Minister, on request or proactively, with data and information needed to prevent or end interference with secure and reliable access to electronic services.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is urgent threat-response guidance to potentially affected service recipients; Norm B is information provision to the Minister for regulatory or protective measures, including on request or proactively, without a specified incident-triggered deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor, recipient, triggering context, and substantive purpose: cyber-threat warnings and recommended measures to service recipients versus data and information supplied to the Minister concerning secure electronic access.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, op grond van artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houders van een erkenning en op grond van artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgevers en diensten verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft om maatregelen te kunnen nemen om inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening te voorkomen of beëindigen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require reporting an incident to a competent public authority, but they do not require the same report: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to report a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority, with specified assessment, indicators, and cross-border-impact information; Norm B requires reporting a narrowly defined serious incident involving certain high-risk AI systems to a designated national authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns significant incidents under the NIS2 framework and requires reporting to both a CSIRT and competent authority with extensive incident information, generally within 72 hours (or 24 hours for the specified trust-service case). Norm B concerns serious incidents involving specified high-risk AI systems and limits reporting to incidents defined in Article 3(49)(c), with no deadline stated in the provision.
verdict.criterion_fired: The shared verb-level action and broad incident-reporting theme are insufficient: the regulated actor categories and substantive incident regimes differ, and the required report content and scope are materially different. The different authority does not itself determine the result, but the actor-role and content differences mean this is not the same compliance work repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit met:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voor AI-systemen met een hoog risico die veiligheidscomponenten van apparaten zijn of zelf apparaten zijn die onder de Verordeningen (EU) 2017/745 en (EU) 2017/746 vallen, wordt de melding van ernstige incidenten beperkt tot de in artikel 3, punt 49), c), van de onderhavige verordening bedoelde incidenten, en wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address handling an ICT/security-related incident affecting data, but A requires urgent notification to the Dutch Data Protection Authority, whereas B requires financial entities to perform integrity checks and reconciliations during incident recovery or data reconstruction.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an external breach-notification duty to a supervisory authority; Norm B is an internal recovery and data-integrity control duty with no recipient or reporting requirement.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A imposes breach notification by a public electronic communications provider to the data-protection authority, while B imposes recovery-stage data-integrity checks on financial entities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij herstel van een ICT-gerelateerd incident verrichten financiële entiteiten de benodigde controles, ook meerdere controles, waaronder afstemmingen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling ICT/AI-related incidents, but A requires financial entities to register all ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats and establish incident-management processes, whereas B requires an AI provider, after reporting a serious incident, to investigate it promptly, conduct a risk assessment, take corrective measures, cooperate with authorities, and avoid compromising later causal evaluation.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing internal registration and incident-management obligation for financial entities; Norm B is a prompt post-report investigation, assessment, remediation, cooperation, and preservation-of-evidence obligation for providers of high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The event family overlaps broadly (incidents), but the actor roles and core actions differ: A concerns financial-entity registration and internal processes for ICT incidents/cyber threats; B concerns an AI provider's immediate investigation and related measures after a serious incident. This is not the same compliance work repeated.

verdict.evidence_span_b: verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating information about consequences of a serious personal-data/ICT incident, but A requires proactive notification of affected individuals, whereas B requires financial entities to provide authorities, on request, an estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ in both recipient and substantive purpose/content: A is urgent risk notification to data subjects; B is an on-request cost-and-loss estimate to competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and materially different core action/content; the shared incident-related context and broad financial-entity overlap do not make the obligations the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: deelt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke de betrokkene de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens onverwijld mee
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an essential or important entity to promptly inform its service recipients about significant incidents affecting service provision. B requires the management body of a financial entity to establish governance arrangements, including enterprise-level reporting channels for obtaining information about ICT-service-provider arrangements, planned material changes, their effects, and at least serious ICT-related incidents and related measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an external incident-notification duty to service recipients; B is an internal governance and information-channel duty imposed on the management body, not a duty to notify recipients of services.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action: A requires notifying service recipients of significant incidents, whereas B requires the management body to establish internal reporting channels and oversee ICT-risk governance. The shared ICT-incident context is insufficient to create duplicate or merely related reporting work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten
verdict.evidence_span_b: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern post-incident information connected with ICT/serious incidents and involve communication to competent authorities, but Norm A requires communicating changes implemented after post-incident evaluations on request, whereas Norm B requires keeping, documenting, and promptly reporting information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a request-based disclosure of implemented changes following an evaluation of a serious ICT incident; Norm B is an ex officio, immediate incident-reporting and recordkeeping duty concerning serious incidents and possible corrective measures for systemic-risk general-purpose AI models.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, actor role, timing, and substantive content: Norm A concerns financial entities disclosing post-evaluation changes upon request, while Norm B concerns providers of systemic-risk general-purpose AI models promptly reporting serious-incident information and possible corrective measures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen delen op verzoek de bevoegde autoriteiten de wijzigingen mee die na de in de eerste alinea bedoelde ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties zijn doorgevoerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an actor to provide information to a public authority, but Norm A is a general, on-request or proactive information-supply duty concerning secure and reliable electronic access, whereas Norm B is a structured mandatory reporting duty for serious ICT-related incidents, including initial, interim, and final reports.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns information needed by the Minister to prevent or end infringements affecting secure and reliable access to electronic services; Norm B concerns prescribed incident reports enabling the competent authority to assess the scope and possible cross-border effects of serious ICT-related incidents.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor scope, triggering event, purpose, and substantive content. Norm A applies to public bodies, designated organisations, recognised holders, issuers and service providers and requires supplying information when requested or voluntarily; Norm B applies to financial entities and requires formal reporting of serious ICT-related incidents to the competent authority under prescribed procedures and models.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, op grond van artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houders van een erkenning en op grond van artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgevers en diensten verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft om maatregelen te kunnen nemen om inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening te voorkomen of beëindigen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling information about ICT/security-related events, but A requires the central contact point to submit a periodic aggregated report to ENISA, whereas B requires financial entities to maintain and test mechanisms for detecting anomalous activities and ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a periodic reporting duty imposed on a central contact point and directed to ENISA; Norm B is an operational detection-and-testing duty imposed on financial entities, with no reporting recipient.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and different core action: A is periodic aggregated reporting to ENISA; B is implementing and testing detection mechanisms. The shared incident-related subject matter does not create the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten beschikken over mechanismen om overeenkomstig artikel 17 afwijkende activiteiten zo spoedig mogelijk te detecteren, met inbegrip van kwesties op het gebied van ICT-netwerkprestaties en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A: notify the affected data subject without undue delay of a personal-data breach. B: establish and maintain ICT-risk-management measures, including incorporating operational conclusions from testing and post-incident analysis into the ICT-risk-assessment process.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent breach notification duty directed to the affected individual; Norm B is an ongoing internal ICT-risk-management and learning-process duty, with no reporting recipient or incident-triggered notification obligation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same underlying action: A requires external notification of a personal-data breach to the affected person, whereas B requires internal ICT-risk-management implementation and incorporation of lessons from tests or incident analysis. verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms respond to an incident by imposing an incident-related compliance action, but Norm A requires internal recovery/data-integrity checks, whereas Norm B requires reporting a serious AI incident to market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an internal technical recovery and data-integrity control duty during restoration of an ICT-related incident; Norm B is an external notification duty concerning serious incidents involving a high-risk AI system, with specified deadlines.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ materially: internal controls during ICT-incident recovery versus notification by a high-risk AI provider or deployer to market-surveillance authorities. The shared broad incident context is insufficient for duplicate or related burden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address security-related events and mitigation, but A requires providers to implement ongoing technical, operational, and organisational security measures, whereas B requires financial entities to notify clients promptly about a serious ICT incident and mitigation measures.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern reporting ICT/security incidents to a competent authority, but Norm A requires a detailed final report (or, under its related paragraph, an interim report followed by a final report) after an incident notification, whereas Norm B establishes the DORA reporting sequence for serious ICT-related incidents: initial notification, interim updates, and a final report using prescribed models and containing information needed to assess scope and cross-border effects.
