verdict.evidence_span_b: dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern communicating information about a security incident, but A requires a progress report or final report to the CSIRT and competent authority, while B requires immediate notification to the Dutch Data Protection Authority of a qualifying personal-data security breach.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a substantive incident progress/final reporting duty for essential or important entities, with detailed incident, cause, mitigation, and cross-border-impact information; Norm B is an urgent personal-data-breach notification duty for public electronic communications providers to the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad security-incident family, but different actor categories, different reporting purposes and recipients, different timing, and materially different required content; therefore related rather than duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in waarin wordt ingegaan op de aspecten, genoemd in het eerste lid
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging, bedoeld in artikel 11.3, die nadelige gevolgen heeft voor de bescherming van persoonsgegevens

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating information about ICT incidents to an external recipient, but A requires providing an on-request estimate of aggregated annual costs and losses from serious ICT-related incidents, whereas B requires making the incident notification (including a voluntary notification) also to the designated sectoral CSIRT.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an on-request provision of an aggregated annual loss/cost estimate to competent authorities; Norm B is an incident-reporting obligation routed additionally to a sectoral CSIRT.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not impose the same core action or content, and their actor scopes differ: A covers financial entities other than micro-enterprises, while B covers specified financial-market actors. The shared ICT-incident context and broadly comparable institutional recipients are insufficient for duplicate burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require proactive cybersecurity risk-management measures, but A requires implementing technical, operational, and organisational measures to control network/service security risks, whereas B requires carrying out a programme of ICT tests (including vulnerability assessments, scans, penetration tests, and other listed tests).
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a general security-risk mitigation duty for providers of public electronic communications networks or services; Norm B is a testing-programme duty for financial entities, with specified ICT testing activities and risk-based planning.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both the actor covered and the core action: A requires implementing security measures, while B requires conducting ICT tests. The shared cybersecurity subject matter does not make them the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: nemen bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur vastgestelde technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van hun netwerken of diensten te beheersen
verdict.evidence_span_b: in de uitvoering van passende tests, zoals kwetsbaarheidsbeoordelingen en -scans, opensourceanalyses, netwerkbeveiligingsbeoordelingen, kloofanalyses, beoordelingen van fysieke beveiliging, vragenlijsten en scanningsoftwareoplossingen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern action triggered by a potentially harmful incident or threat, but A requires the entity to promptly inform affected service recipients about protective measures (and, if needed, the threat), whereas B requires the provider or deployer to make a formal report of a serious incident to the legally designated recipient under Article 73.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a recipient-facing warning/information duty about measures against a significant cyber threat; Norm B is a formal serious-incident reporting duty concerning a high-risk AI system, with a specific death-related deadline and causal-link condition.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, actor role, recipient, and substantive content: A requires urgent communication to potentially affected service recipients, while B requires formal incident reporting by an AI provider or deployer. The shared incident/threat-like trigger is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.
verdict.evidence_span_b: bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern operational responses to risks identified during digital/AI-related testing, but Norm A requires establishing, maintaining, and evaluating a comprehensive digital operational-resilience testing programme, whereas Norm B requires reporting each serious incident found during real-world testing and taking immediate mitigation, suspension, or termination measures.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing programme-governance and testing obligation for certain financial entities; Norm B is an incident-reporting and immediate risk-response obligation for providers or potential providers conducting real-world testing of high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering event, and responsible actor differ materially: Norm A concerns maintaining a testing programme, while Norm B concerns reporting a serious incident and responding to it during real-world AI testing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: voor het vaststellen, handhaven en evalueren van een degelijk en alomvattend programma voor het testen van de digitale operationele weerbaarheid
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the entity to take internal cybersecurity/ICT-resilience measures connected with incidents: A requires a broad, risk-based package of protective measures, while B requires integrity controls during recovery from an ICT-related incident.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a general, preventive and organizational cybersecurity duty covering multiple control domains; Norm B is a specific recovery-stage duty to perform checks and reconciliations to preserve data integrity, including when reconstructing external stakeholders’ data.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident/ICT-resilience context and broadly overlapping regulated entities, but the operative actions and compliance content differ: comprehensive protective measures versus recovery-time data-integrity controls. This is not the same work repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De maatregelen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, zijn gebaseerd op een benadering die alle gevaren omvat en tot doel heeft netwerk- en informatiesystemen en de fysieke omgeving van die systemen tegen incidenten te beschermen, en omvatten ten minste het volgende:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij herstel van een ICT-gerelateerd incident verrichten financiële entiteiten de benodigde controles, ook meerdere controles, waaronder afstemmingen, om ervoor te zorgen dat het hoogste niveau van gegevensintegriteit wordt gehandhaafd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms respond to security/privacy risks, but A requires restricting use of specified suppliers' products or services, whereas B requires promptly informing affected data subjects of a personal-data breach.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a minister-imposed supply-chain/use restriction concerning national-security risks; Norm B is an immediate notification duty to persons whose personal data are affected by a breach likely to harm their privacy.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering-event families, and duty-bearing actor roles differ; similarity in general security-risk subject matter does not create the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: uitsluitend gebruik te maken van producten of diensten van anderen dan de daarbij door Onze Minister die het aangaat genoemde partij
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling or communicating information about incidents, but A requires assigning a spokesperson and implementing a public/media communications strategy, whereas B requires keeping, documenting, and promptly reporting information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures to authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a governance and external-communications role for ICT-related incidents, directed to the public and media; Norm B is a substantive recordkeeping and regulatory-reporting duty for serious AI-model incidents, directed to the AI Office and possibly national competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, actor context, recipients, and purpose: A assigns a spokesperson for public/media communications, while B requires maintaining, documenting, and promptly reporting serious-incident information and corrective measures to authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Ten minste één persoon in de financiële entiteit wordt belast met de uitvoering van de communicatiestrategie voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en vervult daartoe de rol van woordvoerder bij het publiek en de media.
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern making a notification/report after becoming aware of an incident, but A requires a processor to inform the controller of a personal-data breach, while B requires the relevant AI provider or, where applicable, deployer to report a serious incident to market-surveillance authorities, subject to the AI Act’s causal-link and incident conditions.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ in actor, recipient, incident type, and reporting purpose/content: A is an internal processor-to-controller personal-data-breach notification; B is an AI serious-incident report to market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and materially different duty: the GDPR norm concerns a processor notifying the controller of a personal-data breach, whereas the AI Act norm concerns an AI provider or deployer reporting a serious AI incident to market-surveillance authorities. The shared incident-notification form is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern incident-related compliance, but Norm A assigns continuing responsibility for handling and consequences of reported ICT incidents, whereas Norm B requires an immediate formal notification of serious AI incidents to market-surveillance authorities within a specified deadline.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a responsibility/incident-management provision following a DORA notification; Norm B is a time-bound reporting duty for serious AI incidents by providers or deployers to market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying duties differ: Norm A concerns responsibility for handling and consequences of reported ICT-related incidents, while Norm B requires immediate notification of serious incidents. The actor roles also differ (financial entities versus high-risk AI providers or, where applicable, deployers).
verdict.evidence_span_a: blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd
verdict.evidence_span_b: de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responses or follow-up to ICT/data-related incidents, but A requires communicating a personal-data breach to affected individuals, whereas B requires financial entities to conduct post-incident evaluations, identify improvements, and, on request, communicate implemented changes to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent breach notification to data subjects triggered by a likely high risk to their rights and freedoms; Norm B is an internal post-incident evaluation and improvement process after a serious ICT incident, with possible disclosure of resulting changes to authorities on request.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action and actor role differ: A imposes a controller-to-data-subject breach communication duty, while B primarily imposes a financial-entity evaluation, analysis, and remediation duty, with a separate authority-information obligation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: deelt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke de betrokkene de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens onverwijld mee
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, analyseren daarbij de oorzaken van de verstoring en identificeren de verbeteringen die moeten worden aangebracht

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern internal handling of ICT/security-related risks or incidents, but A requires maintaining an incident register, whereas B requires incorporating operational conclusions from testing and post-incident analysis into the ICT-risk-assessment process.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a record-keeping duty covering all personal-data breaches; Norm B is an ICT-risk-management process duty for specified financial entities, focused on using lessons from tests and incident analysis in risk assessment.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor scope and core action: A requires keeping an overview of personal-data breaches, while B requires integrating operational conclusions from tests and incident analysis into an ICT-risk-assessment process. They do not impose the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: houdt een overzicht bij van alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: de relevante operationele conclusies die voortvloeien uit de in punt g) bedoelde tests en uit de analyse na een incident opnemen in het ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling information about incidents involving personal data or serious incidents, but they require different actions: Norm A requires maintaining a register/overview, while Norm B requires making a notification within a specified deadline.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an ongoing record-keeping duty covering all personal-data breaches; Norm B is a time-limited notification duty concerning serious incidents involving a high-risk AI system, specifically where a person dies.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying action and responsible actor differ: maintaining an overview of personal-data breaches is not the same compliance work as notifying about a fatal serious AI incident. The shared incident-related subject matter is insufficient to establish duplicate burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: houdt een overzicht bij van alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions involve communicating information to a public authority in connection with a potentially harmful event affecting regulated digital systems or services. However, Article 19 requires supplying whatever data and information the Minister needs to prevent or end interference with secure and reliable electronic access, whereas Article 73 requires reporting defined serious incidents involving certain high-risk AI systems to the designated national competent authority where the incident occurred.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Article 19 is a broad, potentially on-request or proactive information-supply duty concerning measures to prevent or terminate interference with electronic-service access. Article 73 is a specific serious-incident notification duty for a defined subset of high-risk AI systems, directed to the territorially designated competent authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties do not have the same actor role or the same substantive compliance content: Article 19 applies to listed public bodies, organizations, recognized holders, issuers and service providers, while Article 73 concerns operators of specified high-risk AI systems and a narrowly defined serious-incident report. The shared authority-facing and incident/security-related context is insufficient to establish duplicate work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, op grond van artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houders van een erkenning en op grond van artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgevers en diensten verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen verplichten een aangewezen actor om informatie aan een overheidsautoriteit te verstrekken, maar A betreft incidentrapportage en B kennisgeving van de resultaten van een grondrechteneffectbeoordeling.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A ziet op het melden van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, met eerste, tussentijdse en eindrapporten over de omvang en mogelijke grensoverschrijdende effecten. Norm B ziet op het melden van de resultaten van een voorafgaande grondrechteneffectbeoordeling van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem, met een ingevuld sjabloon.
verdict.criterion_fired: De normen hebben weliswaar beide een informatieverstrekking aan een overheidsautoriteit als kernhandeling, maar verschillen in actorrol, triggering event en inhoud/doel van de verstrekking. A betreft financiële entiteiten die ernstige ICT-incidenten melden; B betreft gebruiksverantwoordelijken die resultaten van een grondrechteneffectbeoordeling van hoog-risico-AI melden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zodra de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde beoordeling is uitgevoerd, stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern recording or reporting an incident, but Norm A requires the controller to document personal-data breaches with facts, consequences, and corrective measures, whereas Norm B requires an AI-system provider (or, where applicable, deployer) to report serious incidents to market-surveillance authorities within the applicable deadline.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an internal documentation duty concerning personal-data breaches and enabling supervisory compliance checks; Norm B is an external, time-bound notification duty concerning serious AI incidents to market-surveillance authorities, with special two-day or ten-day deadlines in specified cases.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, actor role, recipient/purpose, and required content: documenting all personal-data breaches for supervisory verification is not the same compliance work as notifying market-surveillance authorities of serious AI incidents.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern legal consequences or measures relating broadly to regulated digital activity, but A requires an essential or important entity to use products or services from permitted suppliers, whereas B imposes liability for compensable damage caused by GDPR-infringing processing.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a preventive supply/use restriction imposed by a minister to address national-security risks; Norm B is a civil-liability rule allocating responsibility for damage caused by unlawful processing.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying duties, triggering circumstances, and responsible actors differ: A concerns a ministerially imposed procurement/use restriction for national-security protection, while B concerns liability of controllers and processors for damage resulting from GDPR-infringing processing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: legt hij in overeenstemming met Onze Minister een essentiële entiteit of een belangrijke entiteit de verplichting op om in de daarbij aangewezen onderdelen van haar netwerk- en informatiesystemen uitsluitend gebruik te maken van producten of diensten van anderen dan de daarbij door Onze Minister die het aangaat genoemde partij
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een verwerker is slechts aansprakelijk voor de schade die door verwerking is veroorzaakt wanneer bij de verwerking niet is voldaan aan de specifiek tot verwerkers gerichte verplichtingen van deze verordening of buiten dan wel in strijd met de rechtmatige instructies van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke is gehandeld.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an entity to implement and maintain a broad, risk-based package of cybersecurity measures protecting network and information systems and their physical environment against incidents, including incident handling and related controls. B requires data-reporting-service providers to operate systems that check transaction reports for completeness, detect omissions and obvious errors, and request retransmission. These are not the same underlying compliance work.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a broad cybersecurity risk-management and protection duty; Norm B is a specific transaction-report validation and retransmission-request capability.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both their operative action and subject matter: A concerns implementing comprehensive incident-protection measures, while B concerns detecting defects in transaction reports and requesting their retransmission. The texts do not establish the same actor role or a common triggering event.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De maatregelen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, zijn gebaseerd op een benadering die alle gevaren omvat en tot doel heeft netwerk- en informatiesystemen en de fysieke omgeving van die systemen tegen incidenten te beschermen
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a public electronic communications provider to promptly notify the Dutch Data Protection Authority of a qualifying security breach affecting personal-data protection. B requires financial entities to use suitable ICT technologies and processes that secure data and prevent or limit various ICT/data-security risks; it is a preventive technical/organizational measure, not an incident notification.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent, authority-facing notification duty triggered by a qualifying security breach; Norm B is an ongoing preventive ICT-security obligation imposed on financial entities, with no reporting recipient or deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms differ in the operative action, actor role, and event structure: notification of a specific security breach to an authority versus implementation and use of preventive ICT safeguards by financial entities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: maken financiële entiteiten gebruik van ICT-technologieën en -processen die geschikt zijn overeenkomstig artikel 4

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern handling ICT/personal-data incidents, but A requires communicating a qualifying personal-data breach to affected data subjects, whereas B requires financial entities to classify ICT-related incidents and assess their effects using specified criteria.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent external communication duty to data subjects triggered by a likely high risk to individuals’ rights and freedoms. Norm B is an internal classification and impact-assessment duty for financial entities, with no recipient or deadline specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident family and broadly comparable regulated-entity role, but different verb-level actions, purposes, outputs, and recipients; A communicates the breach, while B classifies the incident and determines its effects.
verdict.evidence_span_a: deelt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke de betrokkene de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens onverwijld mee
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten classificeren ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en bepalen de effecten daarvan op basis van de volgende criteria

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an entity to promptly inform its service recipients about measures to take in response to a significant cyber threat, and where necessary about the threat itself. B requires certain small or exempt financial entities to establish and maintain an ICT-risk-management framework and related controls, including incorporating operational conclusions from testing and post-incident analysis into risk assessment. These are not the same compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an urgent outward communication duty to service recipients concerning a significant cyber threat; B is an internal ICT-risk-management and governance duty, including post-incident learning and risk-assessment updates.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms concern the same broad cyber/ICT-risk context and comparable regulated-entity roles, but impose materially different actions and purposes: recipient notification and protective guidance versus internal risk-management implementation and incorporation of test/incident-analysis conclusions.
verdict.evidence_span_a: deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require communicating information about a significant/serious ICT or cyber incident, but Norm A requires the incident to be reported under Articles 26–29, while Norm B requires prompt notification of affected clients about the incident and mitigation measures.

Norm B is a client-notification duty for financial entities, triggered only where a serious ICT-related incident affects clients’ financial interests, and it also covers protective measures in relation to significant cyberthreats.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require preventive ICT/security-risk management measures, including measures addressing the consequences of security or ICT risks. Norm A requires public electronic-communications providers to take prescribed technical, operational and organisational measures; Norm B requires specified exempt financial entities to establish and maintain an ICT-risk-management framework and related controls, including incorporating post-incident analysis conclusions into that process.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A applies to providers of public electronic communications networks or services and focuses on limiting the effects of security incidents on national security or public order. Norm B applies to specified small or exempt financial entities and imposes a broader ICT-risk-management framework, monitoring, resilience, continuity, testing and post-incident learning obligations. Neither norm requires reporting to a recipient, and the specific required measures are not the same.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties are not imposed on the same actor role: Norm A concerns providers of public electronic communications networks or services, while Norm B concerns specified small or exempt financial entities. In addition, the required compliance content differs substantially: general security-risk measures aimed at limiting incident effects versus a detailed ICT-risk-management framework and associated monitoring, resilience, continuity, testing and post-incident-analysis controls.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern recording or communicating information about an incident to support regulatory oversight, but Article 27 requires an incident report to the CSIRT and competent authority, whereas Article 33 requires the controller to document every personal-data breach for supervisory compliance checks.

Article 33 is an ongoing documentation duty concerning personal-data breaches, including facts, consequences, and corrective measures; the quoted text does not itself require sending a notification or specify a deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident-family and actor role, but different core actions and materially different compliance purposes/content: urgent external incident reporting versus internal breach documentation for supervisory verification.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A requires covered public bodies and designated organizations to provide information to the Minister, on request or proactively, to support measures preventing or ending breaches of secure and reliable access to electronic services. Norm B establishes controllers’ and processors’ civil liability for damage caused by GDPR-infringing processing; it does not require reporting, notification, information provision, or another operational compliance submission.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an information-provision duty triggered by the Minister’s information needs or relevant access-security infringements; Norm B is a liability rule allocating responsibility for compensating damage caused by unlawful processing.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, event family, and actor role; Norm A imposes an information-supply obligation, whereas Norm B imposes civil liability for damage from GDPR-infringing processing.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a trust-service provider to report a significant incident affecting its trust services to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours. B requires a financial entity, on request, to communicate changes implemented after an ICT post-incident evaluation to competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an immediate incident-reporting duty concerning the incident itself and its effects; B is a post-incident, request-based disclosure of remedial changes following an internal evaluation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action: incident notification versus communicating post-evaluation changes. The shared ICT-incident context and authority recipient do not make the compliance work the same.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require the regulated actor to take a legally required action, but A requires implementation of security-risk mitigation measures, whereas B requires filing an application for designation with an authority.

verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering context, and regulated actor: A concerns managing security risks and mitigating security-incident consequences, while B concerns submitting a designation application. The apparent similarity is not a duplicated compliance burden.

Norm B requires reporting serious incidents involving specified high-risk AI systems to the designated national competent authority.

verdict.criterion_fired: The core actions and actor roles differ: implementing security measures for communications networks/services versus reporting serious AI incidents to a national authority. The shared security-incident theme is insufficient to create duplicate compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/digital-operational resilience in the context of ICT incidents or incident preparedness, but Norm A requires an incident-related progress/final report, whereas Norm B requires establishing, maintaining, and evaluating a comprehensive digital-operational-resilience testing programme.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a post-incident reporting duty directed to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority; Norm B is a preventive governance and testing-programme duty for financial entities, with no reporting recipient or incident-specific submission.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require communicating a personal/security breach without undue delay, but A requires notification to the Dutch Data Protection Authority, while B requires communication to the affected data subject (subject to the Article 34(3) exceptions).
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The mandatory recipient and compliance purpose differ: regulatory notification to the supervisory authority versus individual communication to the data subject, with B additionally conditioned on a likely high risk to individuals' rights and freedoms and subject to exceptions.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different actor role and recipient/purpose: A applies to a provider of a public electronic communications service reporting a qualifying security breach to the supervisory authority; B applies to a controller communicating a high-risk personal-data breach to the data subject. The shared breach trigger and urgency do not make the duties the same compliance work.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the regulated entity to report a serious/significant ICT or cyber incident to a competent authority or incident-response body, with follow-up incident information and reports under the respective instruments.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns significant incidents affecting the provision of services under NIS2 and, for trust-service providers, requires an initial report within 24 hours; Norm B concerns serious ICT-related incidents of financial entities under DORA, using prescribed models and a staged initial, intermediate, and final reporting process.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same reporting action, event family, and actor role, but the incidents, reporting regimes, required content, forms, and deadlines are not sufficiently identical for DUPLICATE_BURDEN. The possible additional NIS2 reporting channel under DORA does not by itself change the analysis; the decisive distinction is the materially different reporting content and regulatory purpose.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern operational handling of information connected with reported/transmitted events, but Norm A requires an incident notification to authorities and a CSIRT, whereas Norm B requires providers to maintain systems for checking transaction reports and requesting retransmission.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require proactive organisational/technical risk-management measures aimed at digital/security resilience: telecommunications providers must implement security measures, while financial entities must establish, maintain, and evaluate a digital-operational-resilience testing programme.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen betreffen ICT-/incidentgerelateerde compliance, maar norm A verplicht tot onverwijlde melding van een significant incident met inhoudelijke incidentinformatie aan het CSIRT en de bevoegde autoriteit. Norm B verplicht tot periodieke en incident-triggered documentatie en evaluatie van het ICT-risicobeheerkader, plus indiening van een evaluatieverslag op verzoek.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een concrete incidentmelding met een termijn van 72 uur (of 24 uur voor bepaalde vertrouwensdiensten) en voorgeschreven incidentgegevens. Norm B ziet op het documenteren en evalueren van een risicobeheerkader en het op verzoek indienen van een evaluatieverslag; het is geen incidentmelding.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie en de actorrol verschillen: norm A legt een meldplicht op aan essentiële of belangrijke entiteiten na kennis van een significant incident, terwijl norm B een verplichting voor financiële entiteiten betreft om hun ICT-risicobeheerkader te documenteren en evalueren. De gedeelde ICT-/incidentcontext en mogelijke betrokkenheid van een bevoegde autoriteit maken dit niet tot dezelfde compliancewerkzaamheden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit met:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern supplying information in connection with an incident notification: A requires the entity to state whether the significant incident was probably caused by an unlawful or malicious act, while B requires a personal-data-breach notification to contain specified breach information and mitigation details.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an early-warning content requirement for a significant incident sent to a CSIRT and competent authority, including a causation characterization; Norm B is a personal-data-breach notification to the Dutch Data Protection Authority and affected person(s), requiring breach nature, information sources, mitigation recommendations, consequences, and response measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident-reporting context and broadly comparable reporting actor, but the required information and notification purposes differ substantially; the texts do not establish that the same report content must be repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: geeft de entiteit aan of het significante incident vermoedelijk door een onrechtmatige of kwaadwillige handeling is veroorzaakt
verdict.evidence_span_b: De kennisgeving aan de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens en de persoon wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft, omvat in ieder geval de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms impose ICT/cybersecurity-related compliance measures on regulated entities, but Norm A requires restricting the use of specified suppliers' products or services, whereas Norm B requires post-incident evaluation, root-cause analysis, identification of improvements, and—on request for certain entities—communication of implemented changes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a minister-imposed supply-chain/security measure concerning prohibited or restricted suppliers; Norm B is a financial-entity post-incident review and improvement process, with possible disclosure of resulting changes to competent authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, triggering circumstances, actor roles, and compliance purposes differ materially; any superficial cybersecurity similarity does not establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: uitsluitend gebruik te maken van producten of diensten van anderen dan de daarbij door Onze Minister die het aangaat genoemde partij
verdict.evidence_span_b: verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen zien in brede zin op het omgaan met ICT-/gegevensbeveiligingsincidenten, maar norm A verplicht een concrete melding aan een toezichthoudende autoriteit; norm B verplicht doorlopende ICT-risicobeheermaatregelen, waaronder het identificeren en detecteren van anomalieën en het snel afhandelen van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is een externe incidentmelding met een specifieke autoriteit en een termijn van 72 uur; norm B is een intern, doorlopend ICT-risicobeheer- en incidentresponsvereiste zonder meldingsplicht of aangewezen ontvanger.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie, actorrol, ontvanger en inhoud verschillen wezenlijk: melden aan een toezichthouder versus interne ICT-risicobeheer- en incidentresponsmaatregelen. De gedeelde incidentcontext maakt de normen hoogstens thematisch verwant, maar niet dezelfde compliance-arbeid.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: ervoor zorgen dat bronnen van ICT-risico’s en anomalieën in de netwerk- en informatiesystemen zo spoedig mogelijk worden geïdentificeerd en gedetecteerd en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten snel kunnen worden afgehandeld

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern information/reporting channels related to ICT or AI incidents, but A requires an internal governance channel for obtaining information, while B requires reporting a serious incident to a designated national authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A imposes an internal governance and information-gathering arrangement on the financial entity’s governing body; Norm B imposes an external incident-reporting duty for specified high-risk AI systems to the competent national authority where the incident occurred.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and operative action: A concerns establishing internal reporting channels to obtain information about ICT-service-provider arrangements, changes, impacts, incidents and measures; B concerns reporting a qualifying serious incident to a national competent authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over:
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Beide normen houden verband met het omgaan met incidenten, maar norm A verplicht tot interne registratie en incidentbeheer; norm B verplicht tot melding van een ernstig AI-incident, met name bij overlijden, binnen een bepaalde termijn.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft interne registratie en geïntegreerde monitoring/behandeling/follow-up van alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen. Norm B betreft externe melding van een ernstig incident met een hoog-risico-AI-systeem, specifiek bij overlijden, aan een niet in de aangehaalde tekst genoemde ontvanger.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kernactie en actorrol verschillen: financiële entiteiten moeten incidenten intern registreren en beheerprocessen instellen, terwijl een aanbieder of gebruiksverantwoordelijke een ernstig AI-incident moet melden. De gedeelde incidentcontext maakt de verplichtingen slechts thematisch verwant.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a controller to promptly communicate a personal-data breach to the affected data subject; B requires data-reporting-service providers to maintain detection systems that check transaction reports, identify omissions/errors, and request retransmission. These are not the same compliance action.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an urgent breach notification to a data subject, whereas Norm B is a standing technical/system capability for detecting and correcting transaction-reporting defects.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different core action, triggering event, and actor role; A concerns communicating a personal-data breach, while B concerns operating systems for detecting and correcting incomplete or erroneous transaction reports.
verdict.evidence_span_a: deelt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke de betrokkene de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens onverwijld mee
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both concern compliance following an incident and involve an urgent response, but Norm A requires notifying a supervisory authority, whereas Norm B requires the provider to investigate the serious incident and AI system, including risk assessment and corrective measures, while cooperating with authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a GDPR personal-data-breach notification duty to the competent data-protection supervisory authority within 72 hours where applicable. Norm B is an AI Act provider investigation and follow-up duty after reporting a serious incident; its referenced paragraph separately concerns reporting to market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: Norm A requires a controller to notify a data-protection supervisory authority, while Norm B requires a high-risk AI-system provider to investigate the incident, assess risks, take corrective measures, and cooperate with authorities. The shared incident context and authority involvement do not make the compliance work the same.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both provisions concern handling ICT/safety incidents, but A requires monitoring/detection capabilities while B requires reporting a serious incident to a designated national authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a continuous internal monitoring and detection obligation; Norm B is an external notification obligation for specified serious incidents involving certain high-risk AI systems.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same incident-related event family and broadly comparable regulated-entity role, but different verb-level duties and low content overlap: monitoring/detection versus authority notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: zetten voldoende middelen en capaciteiten in om toezicht te houden op activiteiten van gebruikers en het optreden van ICT-anomalieën en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, met name cyberaanvallen
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a controller to promptly communicate a high-risk personal-data breach to the data subject; B requires financial entities to continuously identify ICT-risk sources and assess relevant cyber threats and vulnerabilities, plus periodically evaluate risk scenarios.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is an urgent, event-triggered breach communication to a data subject, whereas B is an ongoing and annual ICT-risk identification and assessment process with no reporting recipient.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, triggering/event structure, and actor role: breach communication by a controller versus continuous/periodic ICT-risk identification and assessment by a financial entity.
verdict.evidence_span_a: deelt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke de betrokkene de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens onverwijld mee
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten identificeren permanent alle bronnen van ICT-risico

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require reporting an incident, but they concern different incident regimes and different substantive reporting duties.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns a significant cybersecurity incident affecting a trust service and requires reporting to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, with specified incident-assessment and cross-border-impact information. Norm B concerns a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system, specifically where a person has died and a causal link is established or suspected; its provision changes the reporting deadline but does not identify the recipient or reporting content.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying verb is reporting, but the triggering event, regulated actor, sectoral regime, and reporting purpose differ materially: trust-service significant cybersecurity incident versus serious high-risk-AI incident involving death. The shared reporting form is not enough to establish duplicate compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require an incident-related notification/report by a regulated entity to an external recipient. Norm A requires the controller to report a personal-data breach to the competent supervisory authority; Norm B requires specified financial-sector entities to submit the DORA Article 19 report (including certain voluntary reports) also to the designated sectoral CSIRT.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A concerns reporting a personal-data breach under the GDPR, with a 72-hour deadline and a risk-based exception. Norm B concerns reporting ICT incidents under the referenced EU regulation, additionally to a sectoral CSIRT, and applies only to specified financial entities; its provision states no deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The reporting verbs and broad incident context overlap, but the actor scope and substantive reporting regimes differ: GDPR personal-data-breach reporting by a controller versus ICT-incident reporting by specified financial entities under the referenced regulation. The text does not establish that the same incident report or substantially identical content must be submitted twice.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A gives an injured person a right to receive compensation from a controller or processor; Norm B requires conformity-assessment bodies to submit an application for notification to the competent notifying authority.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern entirely different actors, event families, and legal actions: compensation for damage caused by a GDPR infringement versus an application for designation/notification of a conformity-assessment body.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family and different actor role, with different underlying actions and purposes; this is not duplicated or merely related compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: heeft het recht om van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker schadevergoeding te ontvangen voor de geleden schade
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A classifies cyber threats as significant; B requires an AI provider or, where applicable, deployer to report serious incidents to Member State market-surveillance authorities, immediately and no later than two days after awareness in the specified circumstances.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a classification/assessment duty concerning the significance of cyber threats based on specified risk factors. Norm B is an external notification duty concerning serious AI incidents, with a two-day deadline and a market-surveillance authority recipient.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ at the core-action, event-family, and actor-role levels: A requires financial entities to classify cyber threats as significant, whereas B requires AI providers or deployers to notify market-surveillance authorities of serious incidents.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten classificeren cyberdreigingen als significant
verdict.evidence_span_b: de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern promptly reporting a security or serious incident, but Norm A requires notifying the Minister and providing all necessary information, whereas Norm B requires the Article 73(1) notification of serious incidents by high-risk AI providers or, where applicable, deployers to the relevant market-surveillance authorities, within the specified deadline.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A covers a breach of the security or integrity of the actor’s own electronic service, or misuse/improper use of access, and requires notification to the Minister plus all necessary information. Norm B concerns serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems and notification to the market-surveillance authorities of the Member States where the incident occurred; its deadline is immediately and no later than two days after awareness under the stated circumstances.
verdict.criterion_fired: The reporting verbs and broad incident-reporting theme overlap, but the actor roles and substantive incident/reporting regimes differ: Norm A applies to a public authority or designated organisation reporting incidents involving its own electronic service to the Minister, while Norm B applies to a high-risk AI provider or, where applicable, deployer reporting serious AI incidents to market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening
verdict.evidence_span_b: de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms address handling potentially significant ICT/security events, but A requires notifying service recipients, whereas B requires financial entities to maintain and regularly test mechanisms for detecting anomalous activities, ICT incidents, network-performance issues, and physical single points of failure.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-notification duty directed to service recipients; Norm B is a preventive/detection-capability and testing duty with no external recipient.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions and actor roles differ: A imposes an urgent notification duty on essential or important entities, while B imposes a detection-mechanism and testing duty on financial entities. The shared ICT/security-incident context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken over mechanismen om overeenkomstig artikel 17 afwijkende activiteiten zo spoedig mogelijk te detecteren

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern ICT/security-incident governance and reporting, but Norm A requires submission of a substantive final (or, under the related paragraph, interim) incident report to a CSIRT and competent authority, whereas Norm B requires financial entities to establish and implement an internal ICT-incident management process covering detection, management, reporting, escalation, communication, and response.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an event-triggered, time-bound external incident-reporting duty with specified report contents; Norm B is an ongoing organisational/process-management duty and does not itself require submission of the same report to an authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms share the broad ICT-incident subject matter, but they impose different core actions on different actor categories: Norm A requires an essential or important entity to submit a detailed incident report after a reportable incident, while Norm B requires a financial entity to design, adopt, and implement an incident-management process.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires an essential or important entity, when ordered by the competent minister, to use only products or services other than those identified as posing a national-security risk. B requires a financial entity to maintain capabilities and personnel to collect and analyse information about vulnerabilities, cyber threats and ICT-related incidents.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: A is a minister-imposed supply-chain/product-use restriction aimed at controlling national-security risks; B is an internal capability and information-analysis requirement concerning digital operational resilience.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms impose different verb-level duties on different actor categories and address different subject matter: restricting use of specified suppliers/products versus maintaining resources to collect and analyse cyber-risk information.
verdict.evidence_span_a: uitsluitend gebruik te maken van producten of diensten van anderen dan de daarbij door Onze Minister die het aangaat genoemde partij
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken over capaciteiten en personele middelen om informatie te verzamelen over kwetsbaarheden en cyberdreigingen, ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, met name cyberaanvallen

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern responding to serious/significant incidents, but A requires notifying service recipients, while B requires keeping and documenting relevant incident information and reporting it to the AI Office and, where applicable, national competent authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The duties differ materially in action, recipients, and purpose: A is urgent customer/service-recipient notification about incidents affecting service provision; B is incident-information recordkeeping, documentation, and regulatory reporting concerning serious incidents and possible corrective measures.
verdict.criterion_fired: The event family overlaps, but the underlying action and actor role do not: A applies to essential or important entities notifying their service recipients, whereas B applies to providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk maintaining, documenting, and reporting information to authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both require the regulated entity to notify affected clients/data subjects promptly about a qualifying cyber or personal-data incident. However, Norm B additionally requires reporting mitigation measures, and its trigger and recipient scope differ.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a provider's notification to the person whose personal data is affected when a personal-data breach is likely to adversely affect privacy. Norm B is a financial entity's notification to clients when a serious ICT incident affects clients' financial interests, including measures taken to mitigate harm; it also covers certain voluntary cyber-threat notifications.
verdict.criterion_fired: Same broad incident-notification pattern, but different regulated actor roles, different legal triggers and recipient concepts, and materially different required content and purposes prevent a finding that the same compliance work is repeated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern operational responses to transaction/AI-system incidents, but A requires maintaining systems to check transaction reports and request retransmission, whereas B requires an urgent investigation of a serious incident and the AI system, including risk assessment, corrective measures, and cooperation with authorities.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a standing systems-and-data-quality control duty for transaction reports; Norm B is an incident-response investigation duty following notification of a serious incident, with risk assessment, corrective measures, and authority cooperation.
verdict.criterion_fired: The underlying actions, regulated actors, and triggering event families differ: A concerns data-reporting-service providers' systems for checking transaction-report completeness and requesting retransmission; B concerns providers of high-risk AI systems investigating serious incidents urgently after reporting them to market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Aanbieders van datarapporteringsdiensten beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both involve assessing risks or impacts associated with an entity's technology-related activities, but Norm A requires ongoing ICT-risk identification and assessment, whereas Norm B requires a user of a high-risk AI system to notify a market-surveillance authority of a completed fundamental-rights impact assessment and submit a template.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a continuous internal ICT-risk-management duty for financial entities; Norm B is a pre-deployment fundamental-rights assessment notification duty for specified high-risk-AI users, directed to a market-surveillance authority.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in actor role, triggering event, operative action, recipient, and substantive content; the shared general theme of technology-related risk assessment is insufficient for duplicate burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten identificeren permanent alle bronnen van ICT-risico
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling information connected with an incident or potential infringement, but A requires supplying information to the Minister when requested or voluntarily, whereas B requires the controller to document every personal-data breach, including its facts, consequences, and corrective measures, so the supervisory authority can verify compliance.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an information-provision duty directed to the Minister and aimed at preventing or ending infringements affecting secure and reliable access to electronic services. Norm B is an internal documentation duty for the controller concerning all personal-data breaches; the quoted text does not itself require a notification to the supervisory authority, although the documentation must enable supervisory review.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in both actor role and core action: A requires designated bodies and other specified actors to provide information to the Minister, while B requires a controller to document personal-data breaches. The shared incident-related context is insufficient to establish duplicated compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft
verdict.evidence_span_b: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Onverwijld kennisgeven aan een externe ontvanger/persoon van een incident of inbreuk die voor die ontvanger nadelige gevolgen kan hebben.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A betreft kennisgeving aan ontvangers van diensten over significante incidenten die de dienstverlening kunnen schaden; norm B betreft kennisgeving aan de betrokken persoon over een persoonsgegevensinbreuk die waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen heeft voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer, met specifieke uitzonderingen en mogelijke interventie van de Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens.
verdict.criterion_fired: De kennisgevingshandeling en het urgente tijdstip zijn gelijksoortig, maar de normadressaten verschillen: een essentiële/belangrijke entiteit tegenover een aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst. Ook verschillen het beschermde belang, de triggerdrempel en de vereiste inhoud/ontvanger: dienstverlening en dienstontvangers versus privacygevolgen en de betrokken persoon. Daarom is dit geen dezelfde compliance-werkzaamheden die tweemaal moeten worden verricht.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A imposes civil liability for damage caused by processing that infringes the GDPR; Norm B requires providers of high-risk AI systems to report serious incidents to Member State market-surveillance authorities, with prompt statutory deadlines and follow-up duties.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a liability/remedial rule concerning compensation for GDPR-infringing processing, whereas Norm B is a proactive incident-reporting obligation directed to market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.criterion_fired: The norms do not impose the same verb-level action or address the same event family: A concerns liability for damage from GDPR-infringing processing, while B concerns reporting serious AI incidents by high-risk-AI providers.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern handling ICT/security incidents, but Norm A requires submission of a progress report or final report to the CSIRT and competent authority, while Norm B requires financial entities to register ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats and establish incident-management processes.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an incident-reporting duty with specified report content and a post-incident deadline; Norm B is an internal registration and incident-management-process duty, with no reporting recipient or deadline specified.
verdict.criterion_fired: The event family is broadly related, but the actor categories and core actions differ: Norm A imposes a progress/final reporting obligation on essential or important entities, whereas Norm B imposes registration and process-establishment obligations on financial entities.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: A requires a processor to inform the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal-data breach; B requires a conformity-assessment body to submit an application for notification to the notifying authority in its Member State of establishment.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The norms concern different actors, triggering events, recipients, and substantive actions: a personal-data-breach notification versus an application for designation/notification as a conformity-assessment body.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different event family and different actor role; the duties are not the same compliance work.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Op verzoek informatie of documentatie verstrekken aan bevoegde/toezichthoudende autoriteiten: A deelt de na post-incidentevaluaties doorgevoerde wijzigingen mee; B legt een kopie van het mandaat over.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: De verplichtingen zien op verschillende actoren en verschillende inhoudelijke doeleinden: A betreft financiële entiteiten die wijzigingen na evaluatie van ernstige ICT-incidenten meedelen; B betreft de gemachtigde van een aanbieder van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem die een mandaatkopie aan markttoezichtautoriteiten overlegt.
verdict.criterion_fired: Niet dezelfde actorrol en niet dezelfde gebeurtenisfamilie; bovendien verschilt de inhoud sterk (post-incident verbeteringen versus mandaatkopie). De overeenkomst dat op verzoek informatie aan autoriteiten wordt verstrekt is slechts een generiek procedureel patroon.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen delen op verzoek de bevoegde autoriteiten de wijzigingen mee die na de in de eerste alinea bedoelde ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties zijn doorgevoerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Hij legt op verzoek een kopie van het mandaat over aan de markttoezichtautoriteiten, in een door de bevoegde autoriteit aangegeven officiële taal van de instellingen van de Unie.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms require reporting an incident to a public competent authority, but A requires a trust-service provider to report a significant incident affecting its trust services to the CSIRT or competent authority, while B concerns reporting specified serious incidents involving certain high-risk AI systems to the designated national competent authority where the incident occurred.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: The triggering incident, regulated actor/system, reporting scope, and substantive reporting regime differ: A covers significant incidents affecting trust-service provision and imposes a 24-hour deadline, whereas B covers only Article 3(49)(c) serious incidents involving specified high-risk AI systems and states no deadline in the provision.
verdict.criterion_fired: The verb-level action and broad incident-reporting family overlap, but the actor role and regulated subject matter do not: A applies to trust-service providers and significant incidents affecting trust services; B applies to providers/deployers or other responsible actors for specified high-risk AI systems that are devices or safety components. The norms therefore do not impose the same compliance duty merely because both involve reporting an incident to a competent authority.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Norm A states that financial entities remain fully responsible for handling and consequences of ICT-related incidents already reported under Article 19(1); Norm B requires conformity-assessment bodies to submit an application for notification to the notifying authority in their Member State of establishment.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is a responsibility rule concerning the handling and consequences of reported ICT incidents, not a new reporting or submission duty. Norm B is an application-submission duty for conformity-assessment bodies seeking notification.
verdict.criterion_fired: Different underlying action, triggering context, and obligated actor: continued responsibility for reported ICT incidents versus submitting a conformity-assessment-body notification application.

verdict.shared_compliance_action: Both norms concern communicating information to a competent public authority following a serious technology-related incident, but Norm A requires disclosure on request of post-incident changes, whereas Norm B requires a prompt serious-incident notification.
verdict.distinguishing_factor: Norm A is an on-request disclosure of implemented changes identified through post-incident evaluations; Norm B is a mandatory incident report triggered by awareness of a serious AI-system incident and causal-link assessment, with a specified deadline.
verdict.criterion_fired: The duties differ in core action, actor role, and substantive content: Norm A concerns financial entities sharing implemented post-evaluation changes on request, while Norm B concerns providers or, where applicable, deployers reporting serious AI incidents promptly to market-surveillance authorities.
